solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', the pH scale

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following species can act both as a Brønsted acid and as a Brønsted base in water?

solution.explanation: HCO₃⁻ can donate a proton (giving CO₃²⁻) and can accept a proton (giving H₂CO₃), so it acts both as an acid and as a base.
solution.why_others_wrong: CO₃²⁻ has no proton to give, so it is only a base. NH₄⁺ can only give a proton. Cl⁻ has no proton to donate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', Brönsted–Lowry acids and bases

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A solution containing CH₃COOH and CH₃COONa resists a change in pH when a small amount of HCl is added to it.
Reason (R): The added H⁺ ions combine with CH₃COO⁻ ions to form weakly ionised CH₃COOH molecules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The acetate ions supplied by CH₃COONa remove added H⁺ as un-ionised acetic acid, so [H⁺] hardly changes and the pH stays almost constant. R is the mechanism by which the buffer works, so it explains A.
steps: Free H⁺ hardly increases → pH nearly constant
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', buffer solutions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
For the equilibrium N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), ΔH > 0, set up in a closed vessel, match List-I (change made) with List-II (effect).

List-I:
A. Temperature is raised
B. Volume is decreased at constant temperature
C. A catalyst is added
D. More N₂O₄ is added at constant volume and temperature

List-II:
I. No shift; K unchanged
II. Shifts forward; K unchanged
III. Shifts forward; K increases
IV. Shifts backward; K unchanged

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Le Chatelier's principle and the equilibrium constant
solution.explanation: Only a change of temperature changes K. For an endothermic forward reaction, raising T increases K and shifts the equilibrium forward. Decreasing the volume raises the pressure, favouring the side with fewer gas moles (N₂O₄). A catalyst speeds up both directions equally. Adding a reactant makes Q < K, so the reaction shifts forward with K unchanged.
steps: Raise T (endothermic) → forward, K increases → III
Decrease V → towards fewer moles (backward), K same → IV
Add N₂O₄ → forward, K same → II
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes either let K change on adding N₂O₄ or a catalyst, or move the equilibrium forward on compression.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', factors affecting equilibria
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The equilibrium constant K_c of a reaction depends on temperature.
(b) For a gaseous reaction in which Δn(gas) = −1, K_p = K_c (RT)⁻¹.
(c) The concentrations of pure solids and pure liquids appear in the expression for K_c.
(d) K_c for N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) has the unit L² mol⁻².
(e) K_c for a reverse reaction has the same value as K_c for the forward reaction.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Equilibrium constants: K_p, K_c and their units
solution.explanation: K_c changes with temperature. K_p = K_c (RT)^Δn, so Δn = −1 gives K_c (RT)⁻¹. Pure solids and liquids have constant concentrations and are left out of K_c. For the ammonia equilibrium K_c = [NH₃]²/([N₂][H₂]³) has the unit (mol L⁻¹)⁻² = L² mol⁻². The reverse reaction has K_c' = 1/K_c.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (c) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', equilibrium constant; relationship between K_p and K_c; heterogeneous equilibria

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A solution is 0.10 M in Mg²⁺ ions. The pH at which Mg(OH)₂ just begins to precipitate when NaOH is added slowly at 298 K is (K_sp of Mg(OH)₂ = 1.0 × 10⁻¹¹, K_w = 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴; ignore the change in volume):

solution.concept: Solubility product and the start of precipitation
solution.explanation: Precipitation begins when the ionic product [Mg²⁺][OH⁻]² reaches K_sp.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.0 is the pOH, not the pH. 4.0 forgets to take the square root of [OH⁻]². 8.5 ignores the [Mg²⁺] of 0.10 M and takes [OH⁻] = √K_sp.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', solubility equilibria of sparingly soluble salts: solubility product

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the reaction A(g) + B(g) ⇌ C(g) + D(g), K_c = 4.0 at a certain temperature. 1.0 mol of A and 1.0 mol of B are placed in a closed 1.0 L vessel at this temperature. The amount of C present at equilibrium is:

solution.explanation: Let x mol of A react. At equilibrium [A] = [B] = 1 − x and [C] = [D] = x (V = 1 L). Then K_c = x²/(1 − x)² = 4, so x/(1 − x) = 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.50 mol would give K_c = 1. 0.80 mol uses x/(1 − x) = 4 (not taking the square root). 0.33 mol is the amount of A left, not of C formed.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', applications of equilibrium constants: calculating equilibrium concentrations

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): At constant temperature, K_c of the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) increases when the total pressure is increased.
Reason (R): Increasing the pressure shifts this equilibrium in the direction of ammonia.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Effect of pressure on equilibrium composition versus K
solution.explanation: Compressing the mixture shifts the equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas (NH₃), so R is true. But the shift only restores Q_c to the same K_c; the equilibrium constant changes only with temperature. A is false.
steps: K_c depends only on T → unchanged at constant T (A false)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', factors affecting equilibria: effect of pressure change
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At a given temperature, AgCl is less soluble in 0.1 M NaCl solution than in pure water.
Statement II: At the same temperature, the solubility product of AgCl is smaller in 0.1 M NaCl solution than in pure water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The Cl⁻ ions from NaCl shift AgCl(s) ⇌ Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ to the left, so less AgCl dissolves: Statement I is true. K_sp is an equilibrium constant and has a fixed value at a given temperature; it is the solubility that falls, not K_sp. Statement II is false.
steps: Common ion Cl⁻ → lower solubility → Statement I true
K_sp depends only on temperature → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', common ion effect on solubility of ionic salts
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the strengths of acids are correct?

(a) The acid strength of the hydrogen halides in water follows the order HF < HCl < HBr < HI.
(b) H₂S is a stronger acid than H₂O.
(c) The acidity of the hydrides of the second-period elements follows the order CH₄ < NH₃ < H₂O < HF.
(d) Down a group, the acid strength of the hydrides decreases because the H–A bond becomes weaker.
(e) NH₃ is a stronger acid than H₂O.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Down a group, the size of A increases and the H–A bond becomes weaker, so H⁺ is released more easily and the acid becomes stronger: HF < HCl < HBr < HI and H₂O < H₂S. Across a period, the electronegativity of A increases, the H–A bond becomes more polar, and acidity rises: CH₄ < NH₃ < H₂O < HF.
steps: (d) False: a weaker H–A bond makes the acid stronger
(e) False: H₂O is more acidic than NH₃
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (d) or (e) is wrong; (a), (b) and (c) are all true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', ionization of acids and bases: factors affecting acid strength

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The average oxidation number of sulphur in sodium tetrathionate, Na₂S₄O₆, is:

solution.explanation: Let the average oxidation number of S be x. Na is +1 and O is −2, and the sum for the neutral compound is zero.
steps: (Structurally, two S atoms are +5 and two are 0; their average is +2.5.)
solution.why_others_wrong: +2 is the value in thiosulphate (S₂O₃²⁻). +5 is the oxidation number of only the two terminal S atoms. +6 is the value in sulphate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Redox Reactions', oxidation number

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The standard emf of the cell Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq, 1 M) || Ag⁺(aq, 1 M) | Ag(s) at 298 K is (E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = +0.80 V):

solution.concept: Standard emf from standard electrode potentials
solution.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode), using standard reduction potentials. The cell as written has zinc as anode (left) and silver as cathode (right). Electrode potentials are intensive, so they are not multiplied by the stoichiometric coefficient.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.04 V ignores the negative sign of the zinc potential. 2.36 V doubles the silver potential because two Ag⁺ ions are reduced. −1.56 V subtracts in the wrong order.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', galvanic cells: measurement of electrode potential

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a galvanic cell, the Gibbs energy of a spontaneous redox reaction is converted into electrical work.
Statement II: In an electrolytic cell, electrical energy is used to bring about a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A galvanic (voltaic) cell converts the chemical energy of a spontaneous reaction into electrical energy: Statement I is true. An electrolytic cell uses an external source of electricity to drive a reaction that would not occur by itself: Statement II is true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', electrochemical cells; electrolytic cells and electrolysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (redox reaction) with List-II (its type).

List-I:
A. 2KClO₃(s) → 2KCl(s) + 3O₂(g)
B. Cl₂(g) + 2OH⁻(aq) → ClO⁻(aq) + Cl⁻(aq) + H₂O(l)
C. Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s)
D. 3Mg(s) + N₂(g) → Mg₃N₂(s)

List-II:
I. Combination
II. Decomposition
III. Displacement
IV. Disproportionation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A decomposition breaks one compound into two or more substances. In disproportionation one element in one oxidation state is both oxidised and reduced (Cl: 0 → +1 and 0 → −1). In displacement one element replaces another in a compound. In combination two substances join to form one product.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange decomposition with disproportionation, combination with displacement, or displacement with disproportionation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Redox Reactions', types of redox reactions
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The limiting molar conductivities of Ba²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions at 298 K are 127.2 and 76.3 S cm² mol⁻¹. The limiting molar conductivity of BaCl₂ is:

solution.concept: Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions
solution.explanation: Λ°m of an electrolyte is the sum of the limiting molar conductivities of its ions, each multiplied by the number of such ions in the formula: Λ°m = ν₊λ°₊ + ν₋λ°₋.
solution.why_others_wrong: 203.5 forgets that there are two Cl⁻ ions. 330.7 doubles Ba²⁺ instead of Cl⁻. 152.6 counts only the chloride ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', Kohlrausch law

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In acidic medium, dichromate ion oxidises Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺ and is itself reduced to Cr³⁺. The number of moles of Fe²⁺ oxidised by one mole of Cr₂O₇²⁻ is:

solution.concept: Electron balance in a redox titration
solution.explanation: Each Cr changes from +6 to +3, gaining 3 electrons, so one Cr₂O₇²⁻ (two Cr atoms) gains 6 electrons. Each Fe²⁺ loses one electron. Six Fe²⁺ are therefore needed per dichromate ion.
steps: Cr: +6 → +3, gain 3 e⁻ per Cr; 2 Cr → 6 e⁻
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 counts the change of only one Cr atom. 1 assumes a 1 : 1 reaction. 5 is the number for MnO₄⁻.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Redox Reactions', balancing of redox reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a neutral or faintly alkaline solution, the permanganate ion is reduced to manganese dioxide (MnO₂). The number of electrons gained by each MnO₄⁻ ion is:

solution.explanation: Mn is +7 in MnO₄⁻ (x + 4(−2) = −1) and +4 in MnO₂. The decrease of 3 in oxidation number equals the electrons gained.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 is the change to Mn²⁺ in acidic medium. 1 is the change to MnO₄²⁻ (manganate) in strongly alkaline medium. 4 is the oxidation number of Mn in MnO₂, not the change.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Redox Reactions', oxidation number; Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The lead storage battery can be recharged and used again.
Reason (R): When a current is passed through it in the reverse direction, the PbSO₄ deposited on the electrodes during discharge is converted back into Pb on the negative plate and PbO₂ on the positive plate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Lead storage battery as a secondary cell
solution.explanation: During discharge, Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) → 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l). The PbSO₄ stays on the electrodes. On charging, the reaction is reversed by the external current, regenerating Pb and PbO₂, so the battery can be used again. R explains A.
steps: Reversible cell reaction → rechargeable (R explains A)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', batteries: secondary batteries
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The standard hydrogen electrode is a platinum electrode coated with platinum black, dipped in an acidic solution in which pure hydrogen gas is bubbled.
(b) When a cell works as a galvanic cell, its emf is positive.
(c) A salt bridge completes the electrical circuit and keeps the two half-cell solutions electrically neutral.
(d) In a galvanic cell, electrons flow in the external circuit from the cathode to the anode.
(e) Oxidation takes place at the cathode.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Galvanic cells and the standard hydrogen electrode
solution.explanation: In the SHE, H₂ at 1 bar is bubbled over platinised platinum in a solution with H⁺ at unit concentration. A spontaneous cell reaction has ΔG = −nFE < 0, so E > 0. The salt bridge carries ions between the half-cells. Electrons leave the anode (where oxidation occurs) and travel to the cathode.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', galvanic cells; measurement of electrode potential

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Given E°(Fe²⁺/Fe) = −0.44 V and E°(Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺) = +0.77 V, the standard electrode potential E°(Fe³⁺/Fe) is:

solution.explanation: Electrode potentials are not additive, but Gibbs energies are. Add the ΔG° values of the two half-reactions and convert back with n = 3.
solution.why_others_wrong: +0.33 V adds the two potentials directly. +0.165 V averages them without weighting by n. −1.21 V subtracts them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', relation between ΔrG° and E°cell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the cell Zn(s) | Zn²⁺(aq, 1 M) || Cu²⁺(aq, 1 M) | Cu(s) at 298 K, the Cu²⁺ solution is diluted 100 times, with [Zn²⁺] unchanged. The emf of the cell (2.303RT/F = 0.059 V):

solution.concept: Nernst equation: effect of concentration on emf
solution.explanation: For Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu (n = 2), E = E° − (0.059/2) log([Zn²⁺]/[Cu²⁺]). Lowering [Cu²⁺] 100 times raises the log term by log 100 = 2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Increases' has the wrong sign: diluting the cathode solution makes the reaction less favourable. 0.118 V uses n = 1. 0.0295 V takes log 100 as 1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', Nernst equation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Sulphuric acid is consumed during the discharge of a lead storage battery.
Statement II: The dry (Leclanché) cell is a secondary battery that can be recharged.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Lead storage battery and dry cell
solution.explanation: During discharge the cell reaction is Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) → 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l), so sulphuric acid is used up: Statement I is true. The dry cell is a primary battery; its reaction cannot be reversed, and it is discarded once used up. Statement II is false.
steps: Discharge consumes H₂SO₄ → Statement I true
Dry cell: primary battery, not rechargeable → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Electrochemistry', batteries: primary and secondary batteries
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In the reaction 2Cu⁺(aq) → Cu²⁺(aq) + Cu(s), copper undergoes disproportionation.
(b) In the reaction Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂, carbon is oxidised from +2 to +4.
(c) The oxidation number of carbon in carbon suboxide, C₃O₂, is +4/3.
(d) The perchlorate ion, ClO₄⁻, undergoes disproportionation in aqueous solution.
(e) The oxidation number of nitrogen in hydrazoic acid, HN₃, is −3.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cu⁺ (+1) goes to both Cu²⁺ (+2) and Cu (0): disproportionation. Carbon goes from +2 in CO to +4 in CO₂. In C₃O₂, 3x − 4 = 0 → x = +4/3. In ClO₄⁻, chlorine is already in its highest oxidation state (+7), so it cannot be oxidised further and cannot disproportionate. In HN₃, 1 + 3x = 0 → x = −1/3.
steps: (d) False: Cl is +7, the highest state
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Redox Reactions', types of redox reactions: disproportionation reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), hydrogen is consumed at a rate of 0.03 mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. The rate of formation of ammonia is:

solution.concept: Rates of reaction in terms of different species
solution.explanation: Rate = −(1/3) d[H₂]/dt = +(1/2) d[NH₃]/dt, so d[NH₃]/dt = (2/3)(−d[H₂]/dt).
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.045 multiplies by 3/2 instead of 2/3. 0.03 ignores the stoichiometric coefficients. 0.01 is the rate of the reaction (1/3 of the H₂ rate), equal to the rate of consumption of N₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', rate of a chemical reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The radioactive decay of unstable nuclei follows:

solution.explanation: All natural and artificial radioactive decays of unstable nuclei take place by first-order kinetics; the rate is proportional to the number of nuclei present, and the half-life is constant.
steps: Rate ∝ number of undecayed nuclei → first order
solution.why_others_wrong: The rate of radioactive decay depends on the amount of the isotope present to the first power, not to the zeroth, second or third power.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', integrated rate equations: first order reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A catalyst changes the Gibbs energy change (ΔG) of a reaction.
Statement II: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A catalyst changes the path of a reaction, lowering the activation energy so that the reaction goes faster: Statement II is true. It does not change the energies of the reactants and products, so ΔG and the equilibrium constant are unchanged: Statement I is false.
steps: ΔG depends only on reactants and products → unchanged → Statement I false
Alternative path with lower Ea → Statement II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', effect of catalyst
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A zero-order reaction has a rate constant of 2.5 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. If the initial concentration of the reactant is 0.50 mol L⁻¹, the time taken for 75% of the reactant to react is:

solution.concept: Integrated rate law of a zero-order reaction
solution.explanation: For a zero-order reaction [R] = [R]₀ − kt, so the time to use up an amount Δ[R] is Δ[R]/k; the rate does not slow down as the reactant is used.
solution.why_others_wrong: 200 s is the time for complete reaction. 100 s is the half-life. 300 s assumes that 75% takes two half-lives, which is true only for a first-order reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', integrated rate equations: zero order reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the reaction A → products, the concentration of A falls from 0.40 mol L⁻¹ to 0.30 mol L⁻¹ in 20 minutes. The average rate of the reaction during this interval, in mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹, is:

solution.explanation: Average rate = −Δ[A]/Δt. The time must be converted to seconds for the unit asked.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.0 × 10⁻³ is the rate per minute, not per second. 1.2 × 10⁴ inverts the ratio. 3.33 × 10⁻⁴ divides the initial concentration instead of its change.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', rate of a chemical reaction: average rate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The rate of a first-order reaction decreases as the reaction proceeds.
Reason (R): The rate of a first-order reaction is directly proportional to the concentration of the reactant, which decreases with time.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: For a first-order reaction, rate = k[R]. As the reaction proceeds, [R] falls, so the rate falls in proportion, while k stays the same. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', integrated rate equations: first order reactions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term in the Arrhenius treatment, k = A e^(−Ea/RT)) with List-II (its meaning).

List-I:
A. Ea
B. A
C. e^(−Ea/RT)
D. Activated complex

List-II:
I. Pre-exponential (frequency) factor, a constant for the reaction
II. Fraction of molecules with kinetic energy equal to or greater than Ea
III. Energy needed to form the activated complex from the reactants
IV. Unstable intermediate at the top of the energy barrier

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ea is the activation energy, the energy needed to form the activated complex. A is the Arrhenius (frequency) factor. The Boltzmann factor e^(−Ea/RT) is the fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Ea. The activated complex is the unstable intermediate at the peak of the energy curve.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange Ea with A, A with the Boltzmann factor, or the Boltzmann factor with the activated complex.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', temperature dependence of the rate of a reaction
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The rate of a first-order reaction at constant temperature falls from 1.6 × 10⁻² mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ to 2.0 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ in 30 minutes. The half-life of the reaction is:

solution.concept: Half-life of a first-order reaction from rate data
solution.explanation: For a first-order reaction the rate is proportional to the reactant concentration, so the rate falls by the same factor as the concentration. A fall to 1/8 is three half-lives.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3.75 min divides the time by the factor 8. 15 min treats the fall as one halving per 15 min (two half-lives). 7.5 min assumes four half-lives.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', half-life of a reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A plot of log k against 1/T for a reaction is a straight line with slope −5000 K. The activation energy of the reaction is (R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹):

solution.explanation: log k = log A − Ea/(2.303RT), so the slope of log k against 1/T is −Ea/(2.303R).
solution.why_others_wrong: 41.6 kJ mol⁻¹ uses the slope of ln k (forgets 2.303). −95.7 kJ mol⁻¹ carries the sign of the slope; activation energy is positive. 11.5 kJ mol⁻¹ multiplies 5000 by 2.303 but leaves out R.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', temperature dependence of the rate of a reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a reaction had zero activation energy, its rate constant would not change with temperature (taking the pre-exponential factor A as constant).
Reason (R): When Ea = 0, the factor e^(−Ea/RT) equals 1 at every temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: k = A e^(−Ea/RT). With Ea = 0 the exponential factor is e⁰ = 1 at all temperatures, so k = A, which is independent of temperature. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Ea = 0 → e⁰ = 1 → k = A at every T
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Chemical Kinetics', temperature dependence of the rate of a reaction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: The temporary IUPAC (systematic) name of the element with atomic number 115 is:

solution.concept: Nomenclature of elements with atomic numbers above 100
solution.explanation: The IUPAC systematic name is built from numerical roots for the digits of the atomic number (0 nil, 1 un, 2 bi, 3 tri, 4 quad, 5 pent, 6 hex, 7 sept, 8 oct, 9 enn) followed by 'ium'. 115 = 1-1-5 → un-un-pent-ium.
solution.why_others_wrong: Unununium is element 111, Ununquadium is 114 and Ununhexium is 116.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', nomenclature of elements with atomic numbers > 100

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: Which of the following elements is a metalloid (semi-metal)?

solution.explanation: Elements bordering the zig-zag line between metals and non-metals in the p-block, such as silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium, show properties of both metals and non-metals and are called metalloids.
steps: Germanium lies on the metal–non-metal border → metalloid
solution.why_others_wrong: Sodium is a typical metal. Sulphur and chlorine are typical non-metals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', metals, non-metals and metalloids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An anion is larger than the atom from which it is formed.
Statement II: A cation is smaller than the atom from which it is formed.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Ionic radii compared with atomic radii
solution.explanation: When an atom gains electrons, the same nuclear charge holds more electrons, repulsion increases and the electron cloud expands: anions are larger than their parent atoms. When an atom loses electrons, the same nuclear charge acts on fewer electrons and pulls them closer: cations are smaller. Both statements are true.
steps: Anion: more electrons, same Z → expands → Statement I true
Cation: fewer electrons, same Z → contracts → Statement II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', periodic trends: ionic radius
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (atomic number) with List-II (type of element).

List-I:
A. Z = 54
B. Z = 92
C. Z = 29
D. Z = 20

List-II:
I. Representative (s-block) element
II. Transition (d-block) element
III. Inner transition (actinoid) element
IV. Noble gas

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Types of elements from electronic configuration
solution.explanation: Z = 54 is xenon ([Kr] 4d¹⁰ 5s² 5p⁶), a noble gas. Z = 92 is uranium, filling 5f: an actinoid. Z = 29 is copper ([Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹), a d-block transition element. Z = 20 is calcium ([Ar] 4s²), an s-block representative element.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange the transition and inner transition elements, or the s-block element with the noble gas or the transition element.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', electronic configurations and types of elements: s-, p-, d-, f-blocks
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The first ionisation enthalpy of the elements generally decreases down a group.
Reason (R): Down a group, the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and better shielded by the inner electrons, which outweighs the increase in nuclear charge.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Trend of ionisation enthalpy in a group
solution.explanation: Going down a group, a new shell is added for each period. The valence electron is farther from the nucleus and more inner electrons screen it, so it is held less firmly despite the larger nuclear charge. Less energy is needed to remove it. R explains A.
steps: Larger distance + more shielding → weaker hold on the valence electron
→ lower ionisation enthalpy down the group
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', periodic trends: ionization enthalpy
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the long form of the periodic table are correct?

(a) The f-block elements are placed separately at the bottom of the periodic table.
(b) The long form of the periodic table has 7 periods and 18 groups.
(c) The elements of group 18 are called chalcogens.
(d) The sixth period contains 32 elements.
(e) All transition elements are non-metals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Structure of the modern periodic table
solution.explanation: The lanthanoids and actinoids (f-block) are placed in two rows below the main body of the table. The long form has 7 periods and 18 groups. Group 16 elements are the chalcogens; group 18 elements are the noble gases. The sixth period (6s, 4f, 5d, 6p) holds 32 elements. Transition elements are all metals.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', modern periodic law and the present form of the periodic table

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of first ionisation enthalpy?

solution.concept: Irregularities in the trend of ionisation enthalpy across period 2
solution.explanation: Ionisation enthalpy generally rises across a period, but oxygen is lower than nitrogen: nitrogen has a stable half-filled 2p³ set, while in oxygen two electrons share one 2p orbital and their repulsion makes one of them easier to remove. Boron (removing a 2p electron) is lower than beryllium and also lowest of these four.
steps: Approximate ΔiH₁ (kJ mol⁻¹): B 801, C 1086, O 1314, N 1402
solution.why_others_wrong: B < C < N < O ignores the drop from N to O. C < B places carbon below boron. B < O < C puts oxygen below carbon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', periodic trends: ionization enthalpy
solution.final_answer: Option C: B < C < O < N

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Metallic character increases from left to right across a period.
Reason (R): Ionisation enthalpy generally increases from left to right across a period.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Metallic character is the tendency to lose electrons. Across a period the ionisation enthalpy generally increases (R true), so atoms lose electrons less readily and metallic character decreases from left to right. A is false.
steps: ΔiH increases across a period (R true)
Higher ΔiH → harder to lose electrons → less metallic
Metallic character decreases left to right (A false)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', periodic trends in chemical properties
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question_text:
Which of the following comparisons are correct?

(a) Atomic radius: Li > Be
(b) Electron gain enthalpy: Cl is more negative than Br
(c) First ionisation enthalpy: He > Ne
(d) Electronegativity: Cl > F
(e) Radius: Cl⁻ < Cl

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Periodic trends in radius, electron gain enthalpy, ionisation enthalpy and electronegativity
solution.explanation: Atomic radius falls across a period (Li > Be). Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative down group 17 below chlorine (Cl −349, Br −325 kJ mol⁻¹). He (1s²) holds its electrons closer to the nucleus than Ne and has the highest ionisation enthalpy of all. Fluorine is the most electronegative element. An anion is larger than its atom.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong; (a), (b) and (c) are all true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties', periodic trends in physical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following elements of group 16 has the highest first ionisation enthalpy?

solution.concept: Trend of ionisation enthalpy in group 16
solution.explanation: Down group 16 the atomic size increases, so the valence electrons are farther from the nucleus and better shielded. The ionisation enthalpy therefore decreases from oxygen to tellurium, and oxygen, the smallest atom, has the highest value.
steps: Atomic size: O < S < Se < Te
Ionisation enthalpy: O > S > Se > Te
solution.why_others_wrong: Sulphur, selenium and tellurium are larger atoms, so their outer electrons are removed more easily.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 16 elements: ionisation enthalpy

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which element of group 16 is radioactive?

solution.explanation: Oxygen, sulphur, selenium, tellurium and polonium make up group 16. Polonium is radioactive and short-lived; it occurs in nature as a decay product of thorium and uranium minerals.
steps: Group 16: O, S, Se, Te, Po
solution.why_others_wrong: Sulphur, selenium and tellurium have stable isotopes and are not radioactive elements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 16 elements: occurrence

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The first ionisation enthalpy increases from nitrogen to bismuth in group 15.
Statement II: The covalent radius decreases from nitrogen to bismuth in group 15.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Down group 15 the atoms become larger (a new shell is added in each period), so the covalent radius increases and the outer electrons are held less firmly; the ionisation enthalpy decreases. Both statements are false.
steps: Ionisation enthalpy decreases down the group → Statement I false
Covalent radius increases down the group → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 15 elements: atomic and ionic radii; ionisation enthalpy
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the hydrides of group 15 (NH₃, PH₃, AsH₃, SbH₃, BiH₃), the strongest reducing agent is:

solution.explanation: The E–H bond becomes longer and weaker down the group, so the hydride gives up hydrogen more readily. The reducing character therefore increases from NH₃ to BiH₃, and BiH₃ is the strongest reducing agent.
steps: E–H bond strength decreases down the group
Reducing character: NH₃ < PH₃ < AsH₃ < SbH₃ < BiH₃
solution.why_others_wrong: NH₃ has the strongest E–H bond and is the weakest reducing agent. PH₃ and SbH₃ are weaker reducing agents than BiH₃.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 15 elements: reactivity towards hydrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The noble gases have high boiling points.
Reason (R): The only forces between noble gas atoms are weak dispersion forces.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Physical properties of the noble gases
solution.explanation: Noble gases are monoatomic and held together only by weak dispersion (London) forces, so R is true. Little energy is needed to overcome these forces, which is why the noble gases have very low boiling points; A is false.
steps: Interatomic forces: only weak dispersion forces (R true)
Weak forces → very low boiling points (A false)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 18 elements: physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group of the p-block) with List-II (general valence-shell electronic configuration).

List-I:
A. Group 13
B. Group 15
C. Group 16
D. Group 17

List-II:
I. ns² np⁴
II. ns² np¹
III. ns² np⁵
IV. ns² np³

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Valence-shell configurations of the p-block groups
solution.explanation: In the p-block the ns subshell is full and the number of np electrons is (group number − 12). So group 13 has np¹, group 15 np³, group 16 np⁴ and group 17 np⁵.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange groups 15 and 16, groups 13 and 15, or groups 16 and 17.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', p-block elements: electronic configuration; Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', groups 15–17: electronic configuration
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about group 15 elements are correct?

(a) Dinitrogen is rather inert at room temperature because of the high bond enthalpy of the N≡N bond.
(b) The +5 oxidation state is more stable for phosphorus than for bismuth.
(c) The basic character of the hydrides increases from NH₃ to BiH₃.
(d) The H–E–H bond angle of the hydrides decreases from NH₃ to SbH₃.
(e) Nitrogen has the largest atomic radius in group 15.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The N≡N bond enthalpy is very high, so N₂ reacts only at high temperature. Because of the inert pair effect, the stability of the +5 state falls down the group; bismuth forms hardly any +5 compounds. Basicity of the hydrides decreases from NH₃ to BiH₃. The bond angle falls from about 107.8° in NH₃ to about 91° in SbH₃. Atomic radius increases down the group, so nitrogen is the smallest.
steps: (b) True: +5 state less stable down the group
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (c) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 15 elements: properties of hydrides; oxidation states; dinitrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The stability of the −2 oxidation state decreases down group 16.
Statement II: Polonium hardly shows the −2 oxidation state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Down group 16 the electronegativity falls, so the tendency to gain two electrons and the stability of the −2 state decrease: Statement I is true. Polonium, at the bottom of the group, hardly shows the −2 state: Statement II is true.
steps: Electronegativity falls down the group → −2 state less stable → I true
Po: −2 state hardly shown → II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 16 elements: oxidation states
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct order of electron gain enthalpy of the halogens, from the most negative to the least negative?

solution.concept: Electron gain enthalpy of the halogens
solution.explanation: Electron gain enthalpy generally becomes less negative down group 17, but fluorine is an exception: its small 2p subshell is crowded, and the incoming electron feels strong repulsion. So chlorine has the most negative value, followed by fluorine, bromine and iodine.
steps: Approximate ΔegH (kJ mol⁻¹): Cl −349, F −333, Br −325, I −296
solution.why_others_wrong: F > Cl > Br > I ignores the anomaly of fluorine. Cl > Br > F > I puts fluorine too low. I > Br > Cl > F reverses the trend.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 17 elements: electron gain enthalpy
solution.final_answer: Option D: Cl > F > Br > I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): For oxides of group 15 elements in the same oxidation state, the acidic character decreases down the group.
Reason (R): The metallic character of the elements increases down group 15.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Trend in the nature of oxides down group 15
solution.explanation: Down group 15 the elements change from non-metals (N, P) through metalloids (As, Sb) to a metal (Bi). Oxides of non-metals are acidic and oxides of metals are basic, so as metallic character increases the oxides become less acidic and more basic: oxides of N and P are acidic, those of As and Sb amphoteric and that of Bi basic. R explains A.
steps: Metallic character: N < P < As < Sb < Bi (R true)
More metallic → oxide less acidic, more basic
Acidic character of E₂O₃ decreases down the group (A true, explained by R)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 15 elements: chemical properties (oxides)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about trends in the p-block are correct?

(a) Electronegativity decreases down group 17.
(b) Atomic radius increases down group 16.
(c) Nitrogen is much more electronegative than the other elements of group 15.
(d) The atomic radius of nitrogen is larger than that of phosphorus.
(e) The first ionisation enthalpy of the group 17 elements increases down the group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: General trends down p-block groups and the anomalous first element
solution.explanation: Down a group a new shell is added in each period, so atomic radius increases and the attraction of the nucleus for valence and shared electrons falls: electronegativity and ionisation enthalpy decrease. Nitrogen, the small first member of group 15, has a much higher electronegativity (3.0) than P, As, Sb and Bi, and it is smaller than phosphorus.
steps: (d) False: N is smaller than P
(e) False: ionisation enthalpy decreases down the group
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) are wrong; (a), (b) and (c) are all true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry (pre-2023 edition), 'The p-Block Elements', group 15–17 elements: atomic radii, ionisation enthalpy, electronegativity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the manufacture of potassium dichromate, a solution of sodium dichromate is treated with a potassium salt so that orange crystals of K₂Cr₂O₇ separate. The potassium salt used is:

solution.concept: Last step in the preparation of K₂Cr₂O₇
solution.explanation: Sodium dichromate is more soluble than potassium dichromate. Adding potassium chloride to its solution makes the less soluble K₂Cr₂O₇ crystallise out.
solution.why_others_wrong: KOH and K₂CO₃ are alkaline and would convert dichromate back into yellow chromate. KMnO₄ is an oxidising agent and plays no part in this step.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', preparation of potassium dichromate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Potassium permanganate forms dark purple (almost black) crystals. These crystals are isostructural with those of:

solution.explanation: NCERT describes KMnO₄ as dark purple, almost black, crystals that are isostructural with KClO₄. Both are salts of a univalent cation with a tetrahedral XO₄⁻ anion.
steps: MnO₄⁻ and ClO₄⁻ are both tetrahedral and singly charged
KMnO₄ and KClO₄ therefore crystallise in the same structure
solution.why_others_wrong: K₂Cr₂O₇ contains the Cr₂O₇²⁻ ion made of two tetrahedra; K₂MnO₄ and K₂SO₄ have a doubly charged anion and two K⁺ per formula unit, so they are not of the KXO₄ type.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate (properties)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
When the pH of a yellow chromate solution is lowered, it turns orange:
2CrO₄²⁻ + 2H⁺ → Cr₂O₇²⁻ + H₂O
The oxidation state of chromium in CrO₄²⁻ is +6. Its oxidation state in the product Cr₂O₇²⁻ is:

solution.concept: Oxidation state in chromate and dichromate
solution.explanation: The chromate–dichromate change is an acid–base (condensation) equilibrium, not a redox reaction. Chromium is +6 on both sides.
steps: No change in oxidation state, so no electrons are transferred
solution.why_others_wrong: +12 is the total for two Cr atoms, not each. +3 is chromium after reduction by a reducing agent. +7 assumes the colour change is an oxidation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium dichromate (chromate–dichromate equilibrium)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The general electronic configuration of the actinoids is [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s¹.
Statement II: The actinoids, in general, show the +3 oxidation state.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Electronic configuration and oxidation states of the actinoids
solution.explanation: All the actinoids have the 7s² arrangement outside the variable filling of 5f and 6d, written [Rn] 5f¹⁻¹⁴ 6d⁰⁻¹ 7s². NCERT states that the actinoids in general show the +3 oxidation state, with higher states also found in the earlier members.
steps: Statement I: the outer shell is 7s², not 7s¹ → false
Statement II: +3 is the general oxidation state of the actinoids → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the actinoids (electronic configurations, oxidation states)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
On heating to 513 K, potassium permanganate decomposes:
2KMnO₄ → K₂MnO₄ + MnO₂ + O₂
The mass of oxygen released by complete decomposition of 31.6 g of KMnO₄ is (K = 39, Mn = 55, O = 16):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the thermal decomposition of KMnO₄
solution.explanation: Two moles of KMnO₄ give one mole of O₂.
steps: Molar mass of KMnO₄ = 39 + 55 + 64 = 158 g mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.4 g takes one O₂ per KMnO₄. 12.8 g takes two O₂ per KMnO₄. 1.6 g uses 16 g mol⁻¹ (atomic oxygen) instead of 32 g mol⁻¹ for O₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate (action of heat)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The E°(M²⁺/M) value of zinc is more negative than expected from the general trend in the 3d series.
Reason (R): Zn²⁺ has a completely filled 3d¹⁰ configuration, which makes this ion particularly stable.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Irregularities in E°(M²⁺/M) across the 3d series
solution.explanation: Across the series E°(M²⁺/M) generally becomes less negative. NCERT notes that Mn, Ni and Zn have values more negative than the trend predicts, and links the values for Mn²⁺ (half-filled d⁵) and Zn²⁺ (filled d¹⁰) to the stability of these configurations.
steps: A: E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, more negative than the trend → true
R: Zn²⁺ is 3d¹⁰, a completely filled and stable subshell → true
The stability of the d¹⁰ ion favours its formation, so R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', trends in the M²⁺/M standard electrode potentials
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with its colour in List-II.

List-I:
A. K₂Cr₂O₇
B. K₂CrO₄
C. K₂MnO₄
D. KMnO₄

List-II:
I. Dark green
II. Orange
III. Dark purple
IV. Yellow

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Colours of the chromium and manganese oxoanion salts
solution.explanation: Dichromate is orange and chromate yellow. In the manufacture of KMnO₄, the dark green manganate is formed first and is then oxidised to the dark purple permanganate.
solution.why_others_wrong: A-IV, B-II swaps chromate and dichromate. C-III, D-I swaps manganate and permanganate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium dichromate and potassium permanganate
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the electronic configurations and oxidation states of the f-block elements are correct? (Atomic numbers: Pr 59, Er 68, Th 90, Np 93; Xe = 54)

(a) The Pr³⁺ ion has the configuration [Xe] 4f².
(b) The atomic radii of the lanthanoids increase steadily from lanthanum to lutetium.
(c) Neptunium can show an oxidation state as high as +7.
(d) Thorium commonly shows the +4 oxidation state.
(e) The Er³⁺ ion has the configuration [Xe] 4f¹².

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Configurations and oxidation states of lanthanoids and actinoids
solution.explanation: For a lanthanoid ion Ln³⁺ the number of 4f electrons is Z − 54 − 3. In the actinoids, the maximum oxidation state rises from +4 (Th) through +5 (Pa) and +6 (U) to +7 (Np), then falls in the later members.
steps: (c) Np shows states up to +7 → true
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) or (e) include false statements; (a) and (d) alone leave out the true statement (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the lanthanoids and the actinoids (electronic configurations, oxidation states, lanthanoid contraction)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The steady decrease in the atomic and ionic radii from lanthanum to lutetium (lanthanoid contraction) is mainly due to:

options.text: The increase in the number of electron shells across the series
The filling of the 5d orbitals, which shield the 6s electrons strongly
The imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another in the same subshell
The decrease in nuclear charge across the series

solution.explanation: Across the series the nuclear charge rises by one unit at each step while the added electron enters the 4f subshell. 4f electrons shield one another poorly, so the effective nuclear charge felt by the outer electrons increases and the size decreases.
steps: Electron added to 4f; nuclear charge +1 at each step
Shielding of one 4f electron by another is imperfect
Effective nuclear charge rises → radius contracts
solution.why_others_wrong: The number of shells does not change across the series. Electrons are added to 4f, not 5d. The nuclear charge increases, it does not decrease.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', lanthanoid contraction
solution.final_answer: Option C: The imperfect shielding of one 4f electron by another in the same subshell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Sodium chromate is made by fusing chromite ore with sodium carbonate in free access of air:
4FeCr₂O₄ + 8Na₂CO₃ + 7O₂ → 8Na₂CrO₄ + 2Fe₂O₃ + 8CO₂
The volume of O₂, measured at STP, needed for 44.8 g of FeCr₂O₄ is (Fe = 56, Cr = 52, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the first step in the manufacture of K₂Cr₂O₇
solution.explanation: Four moles of chromite consume seven moles of oxygen.
steps: Molar mass of FeCr₂O₄ = 56 + 104 + 64 = 224 g mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 31.36 L uses 7 mol O₂ per mol chromite (ignores the 4). 4.48 L assumes a 1 : 1 ratio. 2.56 L inverts the ratio (4/7).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', preparation of potassium dichromate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following ions are diamagnetic?
La³⁺, Ce⁴⁺, Eu²⁺, Gd³⁺, Yb²⁺, Lu³⁺
(Atomic numbers: La 57, Ce 58, Eu 63, Gd 64, Yb 70, Lu 71; Xe = 54)

solution.explanation: An f-block ion is diamagnetic only when its 4f subshell is empty (4f⁰) or completely filled (4f¹⁴). Count the 4f electrons as Z − 54 − charge for these ions (the 5d and 6s electrons are lost first).
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only the common +3 ions La³⁺ and Lu³⁺. 3 misses one of the f⁰/f¹⁴ ions (often Yb²⁺). 6 treats all the ions as diamagnetic, ignoring the seven unpaired electrons of f⁷ ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', the lanthanoids (oxidation states and magnetic properties)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the oxidising reactions of permanganate and dichromate are correct?

(a) In neutral or faintly alkaline solution, permanganate oxidises iodide to iodate (IO₃⁻).
(b) In neutral solution, permanganate oxidises Mn²⁺ to MnO₂, a reaction catalysed by zinc sulphate or zinc oxide.
(c) Acidified dichromate oxidises tin(II) salts to tin(IV).
(d) Acidified permanganate oxidises sulphite ions to free sulphur.
(e) Acidified dichromate is reduced to Cr²⁺.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Oxidising reactions of KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇
solution.explanation: The product of an oxidation depends on the medium. NCERT lists iodide → iodate and Mn²⁺ → MnO₂ for neutral or faintly alkaline permanganate; in acid, sulphite is oxidised to sulphate and dichromate always ends as Cr³⁺.
steps: (d) SO₃²⁻ is oxidised to SO₄²⁻, not to S → false
(e) Dichromate (Cr +6) is reduced to Cr³⁺ → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every option containing (d) or (e) includes a false statement; the only fully correct set is (a), (b) and (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', oxidising action of KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In acidic solution, green manganate ions disproportionate into permanganate and manganese dioxide. How many moles of MnO₄⁻ are formed from 0.6 mol of MnO₄²⁻?

solution.explanation: Mn is +6 in MnO₄²⁻. It is oxidised to +7 (MnO₄⁻, losing 1 electron) and reduced to +4 (MnO₂, gaining 2 electrons). Electron balance needs two MnO₄⁻ for each MnO₂.
solution.shortcut: Electrons lost = electrons gained: x × 1 = (0.6 − x) × 2 → x = 0.4.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.2 mol is the amount of MnO₂. 0.3 mol assumes an equal split. 0.6 mol assumes all manganate becomes permanganate, which needs an external oxidant.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'The d- and f-Block Elements', potassium permanganate (preparation)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl(NO₂)] is:

solution.explanation: Ligands are named in alphabetical order (ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N), multiplying prefixes are ignored for alphabetising, the metal of a neutral or cationic entity keeps its ordinary name, and its oxidation state is given in Roman numerals.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Platinate' is used only for an anionic entity. Placing chlorido before ammine breaks the alphabetical order. Platinum is +2 here, not +4.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The formula of potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II) is:

solution.concept: Writing a formula from an IUPAC name
solution.explanation: 'Tetrahydroxido' means four OH⁻ ligands and '-ate' shows that the complex is an anion. With zinc in the +2 state the charge of the entity is +2 − 4 = −2, which needs two K⁺ ions.
steps: Two K⁺ balance the charge → K₂[Zn(OH)₄]
solution.why_others_wrong: K[Zn(OH)₄] and K₄[Zn(OH)₄] do not balance the −2 charge. K₂[Zn(OH)₆] has six hydroxido ligands (hexa-), and its entity would carry −4.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', writing the formula of mononuclear coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Assuming complete dissociation, how many ions are produced in aqueous solution by one formula unit of K₄[Fe(CN)₆]?

solution.explanation: Only the counter ions separate from the complex; the coordination entity [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ stays intact in solution.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11 assumes the CN⁻ ligands are released as free ions. 4 counts only the K⁺ ions. 2 counts one cation and one anion type rather than the number of ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', difference between double salts and complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Tetrahedral complexes do not show geometrical isomerism, because the relative positions of the unidentate ligands around the central atom are the same with respect to each other.
Statement II: The cis and trans isomers of square planar [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] are optically active.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In a tetrahedron every corner is adjacent to every other corner, so there is no cis/trans distinction. A square planar complex has a mirror plane (the molecular plane), so it is not optically active.
steps: Statement I: as stated in NCERT → true
Statement II: both isomers are planar and superimposable on their mirror images → optically inactive → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', isomerism in coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the uses of coordination compounds are correct?

(a) Ni²⁺ ions are estimated with dimethylglyoxime.
(b) Impure nickel is purified by converting it into [Ni(CO)₄], which is then decomposed to give pure nickel.
(c) Gold is extracted by forming the complex [Au(NH₃)₂]⁺ with aqueous ammonia.
(d) Excess copper and iron in the body are removed with the chelating ligands D-penicillamine and desferrioxime B.
(e) EDTA is used in the treatment of lead poisoning.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT lists these uses in analysis, metallurgy and medicine. Gold (like silver) is extracted as a cyanido complex, [Au(CN)₂]⁻, formed with cyanide in the presence of oxygen and water.
steps: (a) Dimethylglyoxime gives a red precipitate with Ni²⁺ → true
(c) The complex is [Au(CN)₂]⁻, not an ammine → false
(d) Chelate therapy for excess Cu and Fe → true
solution.why_others_wrong: (a), (b) and (d) only misses the true statement (e); any option containing (c) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications of coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The octahedral complex [Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃] is considered. The total number of stereoisomers (geometrical and optical together) is:

solution.explanation: In an octahedral [MA₃B₃] complex, the three identical ligands can occupy one face of the octahedron (fac) or lie on a meridian (mer). Each of these has a mirror plane, so there is no optical isomer.
steps: fac: the three Cl at the corners of one triangular face
mer: the three Cl in one plane through the metal
Both are superimposable on their mirror images
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 misses the second geometrical arrangement. 3 or 4 add optical isomers that do not exist for these achiral forms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', geometrical isomerism (fac and mer)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the IUPAC name in List-I with the formula in List-II.

List-I:
A. Hexaamminecobalt(III) chloride
B. Potassium trioxalatoaluminate(III)
C. Tetracarbonylnickel(0)
D. Diamminesilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I)

List-II:
I. [Ni(CO)₄]
II. [Ag(NH₃)₂][Ag(CN)₂]
III. [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃
IV. K₃[Al(C₂O₄)₃]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Names and formulas of coordination compounds
solution.explanation: In the formula the cation is written first; in the name the cation is named first. Oxidation states in the names fix the charges.
solution.why_others_wrong: A-IV, B-III swaps the two salts. C-II, D-I swaps the neutral carbonyl and the silver salt. B-I, C-IV gives aluminium the carbonyl formula.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Complexes containing chelating ligands are generally more stable than similar complexes containing unidentate ligands.
Reason (R): Ethane-1,2-diamine (en) is an ambidentate ligand.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A di- or polydentate ligand that binds one metal ion through two or more donor atoms forms a ring (chelate); NCERT notes that such chelate complexes tend to be more stable. 'en' binds through both nitrogen atoms at once, so it is didentate (chelating), not ambidentate.
steps: A: chelate complexes are more stable than comparable complexes of unidentate ligands → true
R: an ambidentate ligand (NO₂⁻, SCN⁻) can bind through either of two different atoms, one at a time; en binds through both N atoms together → didentate → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', ligands (chelation)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The coordination number of a metal ion in a complex is the number of ligand donor atoms directly bonded to it.
(b) The oxidation number of the central atom is the charge it would carry if all the ligands were removed along with the electron pairs shared with it.
(c) In [PtCl₂(en)₂]²⁺, the coordination number of platinum is 4.
(d) In K₄[Fe(CN)₆], the K⁺ ions are the counter ions.
(e) A double salt such as Mohr's salt keeps its identity in aqueous solution, like a complex.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each 'en' supplies two donor N atoms, so two en and two Cl⁻ give six donor atoms. Double salts dissociate completely into simple ions in water, whereas complex ions do not.
steps: (d) [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ is the complex ion; K⁺ are counter ions → true
(e) Mohr's salt gives Fe²⁺, NH₄⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (c) or (e) include false statements; (a), (b) and (d) is the only fully correct set.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In metal carbonyls, the metal–carbon bond has both σ and π character. The π bond is formed by the donation of a pair of electrons from:

options.text: A filled d orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding π* orbital of CO
The lone pair on the carbon atom of CO into a vacant orbital of the metal
The lone pair on the oxygen atom of CO into a vacant d orbital of the metal
A filled π orbital of CO into a filled d orbital of the metal

solution.explanation: CO donates its carbon lone pair to a vacant metal orbital (σ bond). The metal then donates electrons from a filled d orbital back into the empty π* orbital of CO (π back bond). The two effects reinforce each other.
steps: σ bond: C lone pair → vacant metal orbital
π bond: filled metal d orbital → vacant π* of CO
solution.why_others_wrong: Carbon lone-pair donation forms the σ bond, not the π bond. CO binds through carbon, not oxygen. Donation into a filled orbital cannot form a bond.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', bonding in metal carbonyls
solution.final_answer: Option A: A filled d orbital of the metal into the vacant antibonding π* orbital of CO

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an octahedral crystal field, the t₂g orbitals point directly towards the ligands and are therefore raised in energy.
Statement II: In an octahedral field, the energy of the eg orbitals rises by (3/5)Δo and that of the t₂g orbitals falls by (2/5)Δo.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Splitting of d orbitals in an octahedral field
solution.explanation: The dx²−y² and dz² orbitals (eg) point along the axes, towards the ligands, and are raised. The dxy, dyz and dxz orbitals (t₂g) lie between the axes and are lowered. The average energy (barycentre) is unchanged.
steps: Statement I: it is the eg set that points at the ligands → false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A 100 mL sample of hard water containing only Ca²⁺ as the hardness-causing ion needs 10.0 mL of 0.01 M Na₂EDTA for complete titration (Ca²⁺ and EDTA form a 1 : 1 complex). The hardness, expressed as mg of CaCO₃ per litre (ppm), is (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16):

solution.concept: Estimation of hardness of water with EDTA
solution.explanation: EDTA⁴⁻ is hexadentate and forms 1 : 1 complexes with Ca²⁺. The moles of EDTA used equal the moles of Ca²⁺, which are expressed as an equal number of moles of CaCO₃.
steps: Mass as CaCO₃ = 0.10 × 100 = 10 mg in 100 mL
solution.why_others_wrong: 10 ppm forgets to scale from 100 mL to 1 L. 200 ppm assumes a 1 : 2 metal : EDTA ratio. 1000 ppm scales by 100 instead of 10.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', importance and applications (estimation of hardness of water)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about stereoisomerism in coordination compounds are correct?

(a) cis-[PtCl₂(en)₂]²⁺ is optically active.
(b) trans-[PtCl₂(en)₂]²⁺ is optically inactive.
(c) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ shows optical isomerism.
(d) Square planar complexes of the type [MA₂B₂] show geometrical isomerism.
(e) trans-[Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is optically active.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Optical and geometrical isomerism in complexes
solution.explanation: Optical isomerism is common in octahedral complexes containing didentate ligands; a trans arrangement has a mirror plane and is achiral. A homoleptic [MA₆] ion is highly symmetric and achiral.
steps: (a) cis form has no mirror plane → enantiomers → true
(b) trans form has a mirror plane → inactive → true
(c) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has many mirror planes → no optical isomers → false
(e) The trans tetraammine has mirror planes → inactive → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain false statements; (a), (b) and (d) is the only fully correct set.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', geometrical and optical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): [Ni(CO)₄] is paramagnetic.
Reason (R): In [Ni(CO)₄], nickel is in the zero oxidation state, and the strong-field CO ligands cause the 4s electrons to pair up in the 3d orbitals, so nickel uses sp³ hybrid orbitals.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Magnetic behaviour of [Ni(CO)₄] by valence bond theory
solution.explanation: Ni(0) is 3d⁸ 4s². In the carbonyl, the two 4s electrons are pushed into 3d, giving 3d¹⁰ with no unpaired electrons. The empty 4s and three 4p orbitals form sp³ hybrids for the four CO ligands, giving a tetrahedral, diamagnetic complex.
steps: No unpaired electrons → diamagnetic, so A is false
R correctly describes the bonding → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', bonding in coordination compounds (valence bond theory)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following octahedral cobalt(III) complexes absorbs light of the shortest wavelength?

solution.concept: Crystal field splitting and the wavelength absorbed
solution.explanation: The energy absorbed in a d–d transition equals Δo, and E = hc/λ. The larger Δo, the shorter the wavelength absorbed. For the same metal ion, Δo follows the spectrochemical series.
steps: Field strength: F⁻ < H₂O < NH₃ < CN⁻
solution.why_others_wrong: F⁻ is the weakest ligand here, so [CoF₆]³⁻ absorbs the longest wavelength. H₂O and NH₃ give intermediate splitting.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory (spectrochemical series, colour)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the octahedral metal ion (with the field strength of its ligands) in List-I with its d-electron arrangement in List-II.

List-I:
A. d⁶, strong field (Δo > P)
B. d⁶, weak field (Δo < P)
C. d⁷, strong field (Δo > P)
D. d⁸, weak field (Δo < P)

List-II:
I. t₂g⁶ eg²
II. t₂g⁶ eg⁰
III. t₂g⁴ eg²
IV. t₂g⁶ eg¹

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Filling of t₂g and eg levels
solution.explanation: When Δo > P, electrons pair in t₂g before entering eg. When Δo < P, the fourth and fifth electrons enter eg before pairing begins. A d⁸ ion has t₂g⁶ eg² whatever the field strength.
steps: d⁶ strong: all six in t₂g → t₂g⁶ eg⁰ → II
d⁶ weak: t₂g⁴ eg² (four unpaired) → III
solution.why_others_wrong: A-III, B-II swaps the low-spin and high-spin d⁶ cases. C-I, D-IV gives the d⁷ ion eight electrons. B-IV, C-III gives d⁶ seven electrons.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting (high spin and low spin)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
