solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', amino acids (classification and properties)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many chiral (asymmetric) carbon atoms are present in the six-membered cyclic (pyranose) form of α-D-glucose?

solution.concept: Chiral centres in the cyclic form of glucose
solution.explanation: Open-chain glucose has four chiral carbons (C2–C5). On ring formation, the –OH at C5 adds to the C1 aldehyde group, and C1 becomes a new chiral centre (the anomeric carbon).
steps: C1: H, OH, ring O, C2 → chiral (anomeric)
C2, C3, C4: chiral as in the open chain
C5: H, ring O, C4, CH₂OH → chiral
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 is the count for the open-chain form. 6 wrongly includes the CH₂OH carbon. 3 leaves out C1 and one more centre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', cyclic structure of glucose (anomers)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar because:

options.text: It is a disaccharide with a molar mass greater than that of glucose
It contains a fructose unit, and ketoses can never reduce Fehling's solution
Its glucose unit has no free –OH groups
The reducing groups of both glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are used up in the glycosidic bond

solution.explanation: A sugar reduces Fehling's or Tollens' reagent when it has a free aldehydic or ketonic group (a free anomeric carbon). In sucrose, C1 of α-D-glucose is joined to C2 of β-D-fructose, so neither unit has a free reducing group.
steps: Sucrose: α-D-glucose C1 – O – C2 β-D-fructose
Both anomeric carbons are tied up → non-reducing
Maltose and lactose keep one free anomeric carbon → reducing
solution.why_others_wrong: Molar mass has nothing to do with reducing power. Fructose itself is a reducing sugar. The glucose unit of sucrose still has free –OH groups at C2, C3, C4 and C6.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Biomolecules', disaccharides (sucrose)
solution.final_answer: Option D: The reducing groups of both glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are used up in the glycosidic bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A salt is heated with sodium hydroxide solution. The gas evolved gives a brown precipitate with Nessler's reagent. The salt contains:

solution.concept: Test for the ammonium ion (group zero)
solution.explanation: Ammonium salts give ammonia gas when warmed with NaOH. Ammonia forms a brown precipitate with Nessler's reagent (alkaline K₂HgI₄).
solution.why_others_wrong: Na⁺, Ca²⁺ and Zn²⁺ do not release any gas when warmed with NaOH.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), qualitative analysis (test for NH₄⁺, group zero)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the flame test, a salt imparts an apple-green (grassy green) colour to the flame. The cation present is:

solution.concept: Flame test for group V cations
solution.explanation: Volatile chlorides of some metals give characteristic flame colours: barium apple green, calcium brick red, strontium crimson red, potassium lilac (violet).
solution.why_others_wrong: Calcium gives brick red, strontium crimson red and potassium lilac.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), qualitative analysis (flame test, group V)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In titrations with potassium permanganate, the solution is acidified with dilute sulphuric acid.
Statement II: Nitric acid is preferred to sulphuric acid for acidifying permanganate titrations, because it is itself an oxidising agent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Choice of acid in permanganate titrations
solution.explanation: The acid used must not react with permanganate or with the substance titrated. Dilute H₂SO₄ is stable towards both. Nitric acid is avoided precisely because it is an oxidising agent and would oxidise the reducing agent being estimated.
steps: Statement I: dilute H₂SO₄ is used → true
Statement II: HNO₃ is not used, because its own oxidising action would give a wrong titre → false
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (redox titrations with KMnO₄)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In a study of the effect of temperature on the reaction between sodium thiosulphate and hydrochloric acid, the cross under the flask disappears after 80 s at 293 K. Assuming the rate doubles for every 10 K rise and that the time is inversely proportional to the rate, the time at 313 K (all concentrations unchanged) will be:

solution.concept: Effect of temperature on reaction rate
solution.explanation: A 20 K rise is two 10 K steps, so the rate becomes 2 × 2 = 4 times; the time becomes one quarter.
solution.why_others_wrong: 40 s doubles the rate only once. 10 s uses a factor of 8 (three steps). 160 s makes the time longer, as if the rate fell with temperature.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), chemical kinetics (effect of temperature on the rate of reaction of thiosulphate with HCl)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Potash alum, K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O, is prepared from aluminium sulphate and potassium sulphate. The maximum mass of potash alum that can be obtained from 3.42 g of anhydrous Al₂(SO₄)₃ is (K = 39, Al = 27, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1):

solution.concept: Stoichiometry of the preparation of potash alum
solution.explanation: One mole of Al₂(SO₄)₃ is present in one formula unit K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O (molar mass 948 g mol⁻¹).
steps: Molar mass of Al₂(SO₄)₃ = 54 + 96 + 192 = 342 g mol⁻¹ → n = 3.42/342 = 0.01 mol
Molar mass of the alum = 174 + 342 + 432 = 948 g mol⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.74 g uses the formula KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O (474) with a 1 : 1 ratio, forgetting that each Al₂(SO₄)₃ gives two such units. 18.96 g doubles the answer. 3.42 g ignores the added K₂SO₄ and water.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), preparation of inorganic compounds (potash alum)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.subtopic: Detection of elements and functional groups
questions.question_text:
Match the functional group in List-I with an observation that detects it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Carbon–carbon double bond
B. Alcoholic –OH
C. Carboxyl group
D. Aldehyde group

List-II:
I. Silver mirror with Tollens' reagent
II. Brisk effervescence with sodium hydrogencarbonate solution
III. Decolourisation of bromine water
IV. Red colour with ceric ammonium nitrate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Each functional group has a characteristic laboratory test.
steps: C=C → adds bromine → bromine water decolourised → III
Alcohol → ceric ammonium nitrate turns from yellow to red → IV
–CHO → Tollens' reagent reduced to silver → I
solution.why_others_wrong: A-IV, B-III swaps the tests for unsaturation and alcohols. C-I, D-II swaps the acid and aldehyde tests. B-II, C-IV gives the effervescence to the alcohol.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), tests for functional groups in organic compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In salt analysis, group II cations are precipitated as sulphides by H₂S in the presence of dilute HCl, whereas group IV cations are not precipitated under these conditions.
Reason (R): Dilute HCl increases the ionisation of H₂S, raising the sulphide ion concentration.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Role of HCl in group II precipitation
solution.explanation: H⁺ from HCl suppresses the ionisation of H₂S (common ion effect), so the S²⁻ concentration is low. Only the sulphides of very low solubility product (group II) exceed their Ksp; group IV sulphides need the higher S²⁻ concentration available in ammoniacal solution.
steps: R: HCl decreases, not increases, the ionisation of H₂S → false
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), systematic qualitative analysis of cations; Class 11 Chemistry, 'Equilibrium', common ion effect
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 0.53 g of an impure sample of sodium carbonate is dissolved in water and titrated with 0.1 M HCl using methyl orange as indicator. 80.0 mL of the acid is needed. Assuming the impurities do not react, the percentage purity of the sample is (Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16):

solution.concept: Percentage purity from an acid–base titration
solution.explanation: With methyl orange the end point corresponds to complete neutralisation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 40% takes a 1 : 1 ratio of HCl to Na₂CO₃. 20% takes four HCl per Na₂CO₃. 42.4% reports the mass of pure carbonate (0.424 g) as if it were a percentage.
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), titrimetric analysis (acid–base titrations)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following tests for anions are correctly described?

(a) Sulphate: a white precipitate with BaCl₂ solution that is insoluble in concentrated HCl or HNO₃.
(b) Acetate: a deep red colour with neutral iron(III) chloride solution.
(c) Sulphite: warming with dilute H₂SO₄ gives H₂S, which turns lead acetate paper black.
(d) Oxalate: decolourises warm, acidified KMnO₄ solution with evolution of CO₂.
(e) Nitrate: brown fumes of NO₂ with dilute H₂SO₄ in the cold.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Dilute H₂SO₄ releases SO₂ (not H₂S) from sulphites; SO₂ turns acidified dichromate paper green. Brown fumes with dilute acid are given by nitrite; nitrate needs concentrated H₂SO₄ (with copper turnings) or the brown ring test.
steps: (a) BaSO₄ is insoluble in acids → true
(b) Iron(III) acetate gives a deep red colour → true
(d) Oxalate is oxidised to CO₂ by MnO₄⁻ → true
(e) Nitrate does not give NO₂ with dilute acid → false
solution.why_others_wrong: Every other option contains (c) or (e), or leaves out the true statement (d).
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), qualitative analysis (tests for anions)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The enthalpy of neutralisation of ethanoic acid by sodium hydroxide is less negative than that of hydrochloric acid by sodium hydroxide.
Statement II: The enthalpy of solution of every salt in water is negative, so a salt always warms the water when it dissolves.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Enthalpy changes measured in the laboratory
solution.explanation: Part of the heat released when a weak acid is neutralised is used to complete its ionisation, so the enthalpy of neutralisation is less negative than about −57 kJ mol⁻¹. Many salts (e.g. KNO₃, NH₄Cl) dissolve endothermically and cool the water.
steps: Statement I: weak acid → energy used for ionisation → less heat released → true
Statement II: enthalpy of solution can be positive (KNO₃, NH₄Cl) → false
solution.ncert_reference: NCERT Laboratory Manual Chemistry (Class 11/12), thermochemistry (enthalpy of solution and of neutralisation)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The phylum Chordata of animals is characterised by the presence of:

options.text: a cell wall made of chitin
a notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system

solution.explanation: NCERT gives the phylum Chordata as an example of a taxonomic category: it includes animals that possess a notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system.
steps: Phylum Chordata: notochord + dorsal hollow neural system
solution.why_others_wrong: A chitinous wall is a feature of fungi, not animals. Jointed appendages are not the defining feature named for Chordata. Red blood was Aristotle's basis for dividing animals, not the feature of Chordata.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Taxonomic Categories (Phylum)
solution.final_answer: Option B: a notochord and a dorsal hollow neural system

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT cites which fungus as an important example of a fungus that causes wheat rust?

solution.explanation: Some fungi cause diseases in plants and animals; the wheat rust-causing Puccinia is an important example.
solution.why_others_wrong: Penicillium is a source of antibiotics. Albugo is a phycomycete parasite on mustard. Trichoderma is a deuteromycete.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Diatoms have left large amounts of cell wall deposits in their habitat over billions of years. This gritty accumulation, used in polishing and in the filtration of oils and syrups, is called:

solution.explanation: Diatom cell walls are embedded with silica and are indestructible. Their deposits, accumulated over billions of years, form diatomaceous earth. Being gritty, it is used in polishing and in filtration of oils and syrups.
steps: Silica walls of diatoms accumulate → diatomaceous earth → polishing, filtration of oils and syrups
solution.why_others_wrong: The pellicle is the protein-rich layer of euglenoids. A plasmodium is the aggregation formed by slime moulds. Peat is obtained from the moss Sphagnum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista (Chrysophytes)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In which organism does NCERT describe true regeneration, in which a fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism?

solution.concept: Regeneration as a mode of reproduction
solution.explanation: In Planaria (flat worms), true regeneration is seen: a fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism.
solution.why_others_wrong: Yeast and Hydra reproduce by budding. A mule is sterile and does not reproduce at all.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World (characteristics of living organisms)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic autotrophs.
Reason (R): Cyanobacteria have chlorophyll a similar to that of green plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Cyanobacteria have chlorophyll a similar to green plants, and this pigment lets them carry out photosynthesis, so they are photosynthetic autotrophs. R explains A.
steps: Chlorophyll a enables photosynthesis → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera (Eubacteria)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Aristotle used simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs and herbs.
Statement II: Aristotle divided animals into two groups on the basis of whether or not their cells had a cell wall.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Aristotle made the earliest attempt at a more scientific basis for classification. He classified plants into trees, shrubs and herbs using simple morphological characters, and divided animals into those which had red blood and those that did not.
steps: Statement II: false, the basis was presence or absence of red blood
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Slime moulds are saprophytic protists.
Reason (R): Under unfavourable conditions, the plasmodium of a slime mould differentiates and forms fruiting bodies bearing spores at their tips.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Slime moulds are saprophytic: the body moves along decaying twigs and leaves, engulfing organic material. R is a true statement about their reproduction under unfavourable conditions; it says nothing about their mode of nutrition, so it does not explain A.
steps: A: true (they feed on decaying organic material)
R concerns reproduction, not nutrition → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista (Slime moulds)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (fungus) with List-II (use or feature).

List-I:
A. Penicillium
B. Neurospora
C. Yeast
D. Rhizopus

List-II:
I. The bread mould
II. Used extensively in biochemical and genetic work
III. Source of antibiotics
IV. Unicellular fungus used to make bread and beer

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Penicillium is a source of antibiotics. Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic work. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used to make bread and beer. Rhizopus is the bread mould.
solution.why_others_wrong: Do not confuse yeast (used to make bread) with Rhizopus (the bread mould that grows on bread).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about members of kingdom Protista are correct?

(a) The cell walls of diatoms form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box.
(b) Diatoms are the chief 'producers' in the oceans.
(c) Most chrysophytes are large, actively swimming organisms.
(d) Ciliated protozoans have a cavity (gullet) that opens to the outside of the cell surface.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Diatom walls form two thin overlapping shells that fit together like a soap box, and diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans. Chrysophytes are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Ciliated protozoans have a gullet that opens to the outside; rows of cilia steer water laden with food into it.
steps: (c) false: they are microscopic and float passively (plankton)
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing (c) includes a false statement; (a) and (d) only leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the symptoms of viral infection in plants listed by NCERT?

options.text: Formation of conidia on the leaf surface

solution.concept: Symptoms of viral diseases in plants
solution.explanation: Viruses cause plant symptoms such as mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, yellowing and vein clearing, dwarfing and stunted growth. Conidia are asexual spores of fungi, not a symptom of viral infection.
steps: Viral symptoms: mosaic, leaf rolling/curling, yellowing, vein clearing, dwarfing, stunting
solution.why_others_wrong: Mosaic formation, leaf rolling and curling, and yellowing with vein clearing are all listed viral symptoms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens
solution.final_answer: Option D: Formation of conidia on the leaf surface

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Viroids were discovered as the causal agents of tobacco mosaic disease.
Statement II: The RNA of a viroid is of high molecular weight.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: T.O. Diener (1971) discovered the viroid as the agent causing potato spindle tuber disease. A viroid is a free RNA of low molecular weight.
steps: Statement I: false, viroids were found to cause potato spindle tuber disease
Statement II: false, viroid RNA is of low molecular weight
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Viruses, Viroids, Prions and Lichens (Viroids)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group of protists) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Chrysophytes
B. Dinoflagellates
C. Euglenoids
D. Slime moulds

List-II:
I. Stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface of the cell wall
II. A protein-rich layer called the pellicle, which makes the body flexible
III. An aggregation called a plasmodium, which may grow and spread over several feet
IV. Include diatoms and golden algae (desmids)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). Dinoflagellates have stiff cellulose plates on the outer surface of the cell wall. Euglenoids have no cell wall; a protein-rich pellicle makes their body flexible. Slime moulds form a plasmodium that may spread over several feet.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Protista
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about fungi are correct?

(a) Fungi prefer to grow in warm and humid places.
(b) In some fungi, the hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm; these are called coenocytic hyphae.
(c) In phycomycetes, the asexual spores are produced exogenously on special mycelium called conidiophores.
(d) Morels and truffles are edible ascomycetes and are considered delicacies.
(e) Asexual spores are commonly produced by members of basidiomycetes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: General features and classes of fungi
solution.explanation: Fungi prefer warm, humid places. Coenocytic hyphae are continuous tubes with multinucleate cytoplasm. In phycomycetes, asexual spores (zoospores or aplanospores) are produced endogenously in a sporangium; conidia formed exogenously on conidiophores belong to ascomycetes. Morels and truffles are edible ascomycetes. In basidiomycetes, asexual spores are generally not found.
steps: (c) false: phycomycete spores are endogenous, in sporangia
(e) false: asexual spores are generally not found in basidiomycetes
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In basidiomycetes, plasmogamy takes place by the fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains or genotypes.
Statement II: In basidiomycetes, karyogamy and meiosis take place in the basidium, producing four basidiospores.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Sex organs are absent in basidiomycetes, but plasmogamy occurs by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells of different strains. The resulting dikaryon gives rise to the basidium, in which karyogamy and meiosis take place to produce four basidiospores.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Fungi (Basidiomycetes)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Chlamydomonas and Chlorella, placed among the algae within plants in the two kingdom system, are placed in kingdom Protista in the five kingdom system.
Reason (R): Chlamydomonas and Chlorella lack a cell wall.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Regrouping of organisms in the five kingdom system
solution.explanation: The five kingdom system brought together Chlamydomonas and Chlorella (earlier placed in algae within plants) with Paramoecium and Amoeba (earlier placed in the animal kingdom) in Protista. NCERT notes that Chlamydomonas and Chlorella have cell walls, whereas Paramoecium and Amoeba lack them, so R is false.
steps: R: false, both have cell walls
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Introduction (five kingdom classification)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (organism) with List-II (kingdom in Whittaker's system).

List-I:
A. Nostoc
B. Paramoecium
C. Yeast
D. Cuscuta

List-II:
I. Fungi
II. Plantae
III. Monera
IV. Protista

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Placing organisms in the five kingdoms
solution.explanation: Nostoc is a cyanobacterium (Monera). Paramoecium, earlier placed among animals, is a protist. Yeast is a unicellular fungus. Cuscuta is a parasite, yet it is a member of Plantae, which also includes a few partially heterotrophic members.
solution.why_others_wrong: Being unicellular does not make yeast a protist, and being parasitic does not remove Cuscuta from Plantae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biological Classification', Kingdom Monera; Kingdom Protista; Kingdom Fungi; Kingdom Plantae
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about living organisms are correct?

(a) Living organisms grow from inside, whereas non-living objects such as mountains and sand mounds grow by accumulation of material on their surface.
(b) Growth is a defining property of living organisms, without any exception.
(c) Fungi, filamentous algae and the protonema of mosses easily multiply by fragmentation.
(d) The number of species that are known and described ranges between 1.7 and 1.8 million.
(e) All organisms, from prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes, can sense and respond to environmental cues.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Growth in living organisms is from inside, unlike the surface accumulation by which mountains and sand mounds grow. Because non-living objects also grow in mass, growth cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms. Fungi, filamentous algae and moss protonema multiply by fragmentation. About 1.7–1.8 million species are known and described. All organisms sense and respond to environmental cues.
steps: (b) false: growth is not a defining property
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) contain a false statement; (c), (d) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'The Living World', Diversity in the Living World

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Green algae may have discoid, plate-like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral or ribbon-shaped chloroplasts. The major pigments localised in these chloroplasts are:

options.text: chlorophyll a and c with fucoxanthin
chlorophyll a and d with phycoerythrin

solution.explanation: Members of Chlorophyceae are grass green because chlorophyll a and b dominate; these pigments are localised in definite chloroplasts of varied shapes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Chlorophyll a and c with fucoxanthin is the brown-algal set; chlorophyll a and d with phycoerythrin is the red-algal set; floridean starch is a stored food, not a pigment.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Chlorophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: chlorophyll a and b

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mosses, along with lichens, are the first organisms to colonise:

solution.explanation: Mosses, along with lichens, are the first organisms to colonise rocks and are therefore of great ecological importance. They decompose rocks, making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants.
steps: Pioneers on rocks: lichens and mosses
solution.why_others_wrong: The other habitats are not the ones NCERT names for these pioneer organisms.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Horsetails and ferns belong to the group:

solution.explanation: The pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. They are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders, and many are grown as ornamentals.
solution.why_others_wrong: Bryophytes are liverworts and mosses; gymnosperms bear naked seeds; Phaeophyceae are brown algae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In Cycas, the pinnate leaves:

options.text: are shed within a few weeks
are reduced to scales without chlorophyll
are produced only on underground stems

solution.explanation: Gymnosperm leaves may be simple or compound. In Cycas, the pinnate leaves persist for a few years.
steps: Cycas: pinnate leaves that persist for a few years
solution.why_others_wrong: None of the other descriptions is given for Cycas leaves; its stem is unbranched and aerial, bearing a crown of pinnate leaves.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option D: persist for a few years

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (group).

List-I:
A. Polysiphonia
B. Chara
C. Ectocarpus
D. Polytrichum

List-II:
I. Red alga
II. Brown alga
III. Green alga
IV. Moss

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Polysiphonia is a red alga (Rhodophyceae), Chara a green alga (Chlorophyceae), Ectocarpus a brown alga (Phaeophyceae) and Polytrichum a moss.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae; Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The majority of red algae are marine, with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas.
Statement II: Floridean starch, the stored food of red algae, is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Most red algae are marine, with greater concentrations in warmer areas. Their food is stored as floridean starch, which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Rhodophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mosses play an important role in preventing soil erosion.
Reason (R): Mosses form dense mats on the soil, which reduce the impact of falling rain.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Since mosses form dense mats on the soil, they reduce the impact of falling rain and so prevent soil erosion. R gives the reason for A.
steps: Dense mats soften the impact of rain → less erosion → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about gymnosperms are correct?

(a) Their leaves are well adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind.
(b) The pollen grains develop within the microsporangia.
(c) The megaspore mother cell divides mitotically to form four megaspores.
(d) The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards the archegonia in the ovules.
(e) The multicellular female gametophyte is shed from the megasporangium before fertilisation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Gymnosperm leaves withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. Microspores develop into reduced male gametophytes, the pollen grains, within the microsporangia. The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores. The female gametophyte is retained within the megasporangium, and the pollen tube carries the male gametes towards its archegonia.
steps: (e) false: the female gametophyte is retained within the megasporangium
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places, and none of them can grow in sandy soil.
Statement II: The leaves of all pteridophytes are large macrophylls.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places, though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. Their leaves are small (microphylls, as in Selaginella) or large (macrophylls, as in ferns).
steps: Statement I: false, some flourish in sandy soil
Statement II: false, some have microphylls
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Pteridophytes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Members of Rhodophyceae owe their red colour to the pigment fucoxanthin.
Reason (R): Members of Rhodophyceae have a predominance of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin in their body.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Red algae are red because of the predominance of r-phycoerythrin. Fucoxanthin is the pigment whose amount decides the colour of brown algae, so A is false.
steps: A: false, fucoxanthin is the brown-algal pigment
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Rhodophyceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In leafy liverworts, the tiny leaf-like appendages are:

options.text: arranged spirally on upright, slender axes
borne in whorls at each node
arranged in two rows on the stem-like structures
borne as a rosette on a creeping protonema

solution.explanation: The thallus of liverworts such as Marchantia is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy members have tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows on the stem-like structures.
steps: Leafy liverworts: two rows of leaf-like appendages
Mosses: spirally arranged leaves on upright axes
solution.why_others_wrong: Spirally arranged leaves on upright, slender axes describe the leafy stage of mosses. Whorls and a rosette on a protonema are not described for liverworts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (Liverworts)
solution.final_answer: Option C: arranged in two rows on the stem-like structures

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure in a gymnosperm) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Microsporophyll
B. Megasporophyll
C. Archegonium
D. Pollen grain

List-II:
I. Represents the highly reduced male gametophyte
II. Bears the microsporangia
III. Bears the ovules
IV. Two or more of these are borne by the multicellular female gametophyte

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Microsporophylls bear microsporangia, in which the microspores develop into the reduced male gametophyte, the pollen grain. Ovules are borne on megasporophylls. The female gametophyte, retained inside the megasporangium, bears two or more archegonia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Gymnosperms
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant group) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Chlorophyceae
B. Phaeophyceae
C. Rhodophyceae
D. Mosses

List-II:
I. Cell wall of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters
II. Rigid cell wall with an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose
III. Cellulosic cell wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin
IV. Multicellular, branched rhizoids

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Green algae have a rigid wall with an inner cellulose layer and an outer pectose layer. Brown algae have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by algin. Red algae have walls of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. Mosses are attached to the substratum by multicellular, branched rhizoids.
solution.why_others_wrong: Algin belongs with brown algae and polysulphate esters with red algae; the options that swap them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae (Table: Divisions of Algae and their main characteristics); Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about reproduction in algae are correct?

(a) In Ulothrix, fusion takes place between flagellated gametes that are similar in size.
(b) The gametes of brown algae are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella.
(c) In red algae, sexual reproduction is oogamous and is accompanied by complex post-fertilisation developments.
(d) In red algae, asexual reproduction takes place by motile zoospores.
(e) In brown algae, the union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Ulothrix is isogamous with flagellated gametes. Brown-algal gametes are pear-shaped with two laterally attached flagella, and they unite in water or within the oogonium. Red algae reproduce asexually by non-motile spores and sexually by non-motile gametes; sexual reproduction is oogamous with complex post-fertilisation developments.
steps: (d) false: red algae form non-motile spores
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Algae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In liverworts, the male and female sex organs are always produced on different thalli.
Statement II: In liverworts, the sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule, and spores are produced within the capsule after meiosis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In liverworts, the male and female sex organs are produced either on the same or on different thalli. The sporophyte has a foot, seta and capsule, and spores are produced in the capsule after meiosis.
steps: Statement I: false, they may be on the same or different thalli
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes (Liverworts)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sphagnum provides peat that has long been used as fuel.
Reason (R): Sphagnum is a liverwort.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Some mosses like Sphagnum provide peat that has long been used as fuel. Sphagnum is a moss, like Funaria and Polytrichum, not a liverwort, so R is false.
steps: R: false, Sphagnum is a moss
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about bryophytes are correct?

(a) They lack true roots, stem or leaves, though they may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures.
(b) Some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals and birds.
(c) Liverworts grow in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil and the bark of trees.
(d) The thallus of Marchantia is erect and radially symmetrical.
(e) The zygote develops into a multicellular body called the sporophyte.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Bryophytes lack true roots, stems and leaves. Some mosses are food for herbaceous mammals and birds. Liverworts grow in moist, shady habitats. The thallus of Marchantia is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The zygote develops into a multicellular sporophyte.
steps: (d) false: the thallus is dorsiventral and appressed
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a), (c) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Plant Kingdom', Bryophytes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which region of the root is responsible for the growth of the root in length?

solution.explanation: The cells just proximal to the region of meristematic activity undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length; this is the region of elongation.
steps: Elongation region: rapid elongation → growth in length
solution.why_others_wrong: The root cap protects the root apex. The meristematic region produces new cells but NCERT attributes growth in length to the region of elongation. Root hairs arise in the region of maturation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root (Regions of the root)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Long, thin, flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in the wind. This:

options.text: cools the leaf and brings fresh air to the leaf surface
stores reserve food in the petiole
helps the plant climb a support
protects the axillary bud from grazing animals

solution.explanation: The petiole helps hold the blade to light. Long, thin, flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in the wind, thereby cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to the leaf surface.
steps: Fluttering blade → cooling + fresh air at the leaf surface
solution.why_others_wrong: None of the other functions is attributed to fluttering petioles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option A: cools the leaf and brings fresh air to the leaf surface

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A flower that can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane is described as:

solution.explanation: When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane through the centre, it is actinomorphic (radial symmetry). When it can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic (bilateral symmetry). A flower that cannot be divided into similar halves by any vertical plane is asymmetric.
steps: One plane only → zygomorphic (e.g. pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia)
solution.why_others_wrong: Actinomorphic (radially symmetrical) flowers can be halved in any radial plane; asymmetric flowers cannot be halved in any plane.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A fruit formed without fertilisation of the ovary is called a:

solution.explanation: The fruit is a mature or ripened ovary developed after fertilisation. If a fruit is formed without fertilisation of the ovary, it is called a parthenocarpic fruit.
solution.why_others_wrong: Drupe, legume and berry are fruit types named for their structure, not for fruit formation without fertilisation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Fruit

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which pair of plants of the family Fabaceae is a source of edible oil?

solution.explanation: Many Fabaceae plants are sources of pulses, and soyabean and groundnut are sources of edible oil. Sesbania and Trifolium give fodder, lupin and sweet pea are ornamentals, Indigofera gives a dye and sunhemp gives fibre.
solution.why_others_wrong: Sesbania and Trifolium are fodder plants; lupin and sweet pea are ornamentals; Indigofera is a dye and sunhemp a fibre plant.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae: economic importance)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In flowers such as Salvia and mustard, the stamens of the same flower vary in the length of their filaments.
Statement II: In lotus and rose, the carpels of the gynoecium are free (apocarpous).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Stamens of a flower may vary in filament length, as in Salvia and mustard. When the carpels are free, as in lotus and rose, the gynoecium is apocarpous; when fused, as in mustard and tomato, it is syncarpous.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower (Androecium; Gynoecium)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a compound leaf, a bud is present in the axil of each leaflet.
Reason (R): In both simple and compound leaves, a bud is present in the axil of the petiole.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A bud is present in the axil of the petiole in both simple and compound leaves, but not in the axil of the leaflets of a compound leaf. This is how a compound leaf is told apart from a branch bearing leaves.
steps: A: false, leaflets have no axillary buds
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf (Types of leaves)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Bracteate
B. Trimerous
C. Staminode
D. Polyandrous

List-II:
I. Floral appendages in multiples of three
II. A sterile stamen
III. Stamens free from one another
IV. Flowers with a reduced leaf found at the base of the pedicel

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Flowers with bracts (reduced leaves at the base of the pedicel) are bracteate. A trimerous flower has its floral appendages in multiples of three. A sterile stamen is a staminode. Stamens that are free are called polyandrous.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about seeds are correct?

(a) In castor, the endosperm formed as a result of double fertilisation is a food-storing tissue.
(b) In cereals such as maize, the endosperm is bulky and stores food.
(c) In cereals, the seed coat is membranous and generally fused with the fruit wall.
(d) The cotyledons of a dicotyledonous seed are thin and papery and contain no reserve food.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In castor, the endosperm formed by double fertilisation stores food. In cereals such as maize, the seed coat is membranous and fused with the fruit wall, and the endosperm is bulky and stores food. In dicot seeds, the cotyledons are often fleshy and full of reserve food.
steps: (d) false: cotyledons are often fleshy, with reserve food
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a) and (b) only leaves out the true statement (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Seed (Structure of a dicotyledonous seed; Structure of a monocotyledonous seed)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a simple leaf, the incisions of the lamina, if any, do not touch the midrib.
Statement II: The leaves of the pitcher plant and Venus fly trap are modified to store water.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A leaf is simple when its lamina is entire or, when incised, the incisions do not touch the midrib. The leaves of insectivorous plants such as the pitcher plant and Venus fly trap are modified to trap insects, not to store water.
steps: Statement II: false, they are modified leaves of insectivorous plants
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Leaf (Types of leaves; Modifications of leaves)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The family Fabaceae was earlier called Papilionoideae, a subfamily of the family Leguminosae.
Reason (R): Plants of the family Fabaceae have roots with root nodules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are true. A is about the history of the family's name, while R is a vegetative character of its members; root nodules do not explain why the family was once called Papilionoideae.
steps: R is an unrelated character → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant of Liliaceae) with List-II (use).

List-I:
A. Tulip
B. Aloe
C. Asparagus
D. Colchicum autumnale

List-II:
I. Vegetable
II. Source of colchicine
III. Ornamental
IV. Medicine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Many Liliaceae plants are ornamentals (tulip, Gloriosa), sources of medicine (Aloe) and vegetables (Asparagus); colchicine is obtained from Colchicum autumnale.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Liliaceae: economic importance)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about flowers are correct?

(a) In vexillary aestivation, the largest petal (standard) overlaps the two lateral petals (wings), which in turn overlap the two smallest anterior petals (keel).
(b) Vexillary aestivation is found in pea and bean flowers.
(c) The ray florets of sunflower are epigynous.
(d) Each anther lobe usually has four chambers, the pollen sacs.
(e) Lemon shows parietal placentation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In pea and bean, the standard overlaps the wings, which overlap the keel: vexillary (papilionaceous) aestivation. The ray florets of sunflower are epigynous. A typical anther is bilobed, and each lobe has two chambers (pollen sacs). Lemon, like china rose and tomato, has axile placentation.
steps: (d) false: each lobe has two chambers
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Flower

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the symbols used in a floral formula are correct?

(a) Br stands for bracteate.
(b) ⊕ indicates an actinomorphic flower and % a zygomorphic flower.
(c) A superior ovary is indicated by a line drawn above the symbol G.
(d) Fusion of parts is indicated by enclosing the figure within brackets.
(e) Adhesion is indicated by a line drawn above the symbols of the floral parts.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Semi-technical description of a flowering plant
solution.explanation: In a floral formula, Br stands for bracteate, K for calyx, C for corolla, P for perianth, A for androecium and G for gynoecium. G with a line below it shows a superior ovary and G with a line above it an inferior ovary. ⊕ shows an actinomorphic flower and % a zygomorphic one. Fusion is shown by brackets and adhesion by a line drawn above the symbols of the floral parts.
steps: (c) false: a line above G means an inferior ovary
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) contain a false statement; (b), (d) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Semi-technical Description of a Typical Flowering Plant

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (plant) with List-II (family and use).

List-I:
A. Lupin
B. Petunia
C. Trifolium
D. Tobacco

List-II:
I. Fodder plant of Fabaceae
II. Fumigatory of Solanaceae
III. Ornamental of Fabaceae
IV. Ornamental of Solanaceae

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Economic importance of Fabaceae and Solanaceae
solution.explanation: Lupin and sweet pea are ornamental Fabaceae; Sesbania and Trifolium are Fabaceae fodder plants. Petunia is an ornamental of Solanaceae and tobacco is its fumigatory.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each row needs both the family and the use; lupin and petunia are both ornamentals, but from different families.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Fabaceae; Solanaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the family Solanaceae, the stem is always woody.
Reason (R): In potato (Solanum tuberosum), a member of Solanaceae, the stem is underground.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Solanaceae plants are mostly herbs and shrubs; the stem is herbaceous, rarely woody, and in potato it is underground. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false, the stem is herbaceous, rarely woody
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', Description of Some Important Families (Solanaceae)
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Colocasia stores food in swollen roots.
Statement II: Carrot stores food in a swollen tap root.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The underground stems of potato, ginger, turmeric, zaminkand and Colocasia are modified to store food. The tap roots of carrot and turnip, and the adventitious roots of sweet potato, get swollen and store food.
steps: Statement I: false, Colocasia stores food in an underground stem
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Morphology of Flowering Plants', The Root (Modifications of root); The Stem (Modifications of stem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The innermost layer of the cortex in a dicot root is the:

solution.explanation: In a dicot root, the cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells, and its innermost layer is the endodermis. The pericycle lies next to the endodermis, on its inner side.
steps: Epiblema → cortex → endodermis (innermost cortex) → pericycle → vascular tissue
solution.why_others_wrong: The pericycle lies inside the endodermis and is not part of the cortex. The epiblema is the outermost layer. Hypodermis is described for stems, below the epidermis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants (Dicotyledonous root)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Phloem fibres are also called:

solution.explanation: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. They are much elongated and unbranched, with pointed, needle-like apices.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tracheids are xylem elements, sclereids are short sclerenchyma cells, and companion cells are living parenchymatous cells of phloem.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Phloem)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the conjoint vascular bundles of stems and leaves, the phloem is usually located:

options.text: only on the inner side of the xylem
on alternate radii with the xylem
only on the outer side of the xylem
in the centre, surrounded by the xylem

solution.explanation: In conjoint vascular bundles, xylem and phloem are jointly situated on the same radius. They are common in stems and leaves, and the phloem is usually located only on the outer side of the xylem.
steps: Conjoint: same radius; phloem usually outside the xylem
solution.why_others_wrong: Xylem and phloem on alternate radii describes radial bundles of roots. The other positions are not described for conjoint bundles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (Vascular tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option C: only on the outer side of the xylem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Xylem and phloem together constitute the vascular bundles.
Statement II: All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis, such as the pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, constitute the stele.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The vascular system consists of complex tissues, phloem and xylem, which together form vascular bundles. All tissues on the inner side of the endodermis (pericycle, vascular bundles and pith) form the stele.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System; Anatomy of Dicotyledonous Root
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Collenchyma provides mechanical support mainly to:

options.text: growing parts of the plant, such as the young stem and the petiole of a leaf
the hard seed coats of legumes
the dead, central wood of old tree trunks

solution.explanation: Collenchyma occurs in layers below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants. Its cells are thickened at the corners with cellulose, hemicellulose and pectin, often contain chloroplasts, and provide mechanical support to growing parts such as the young stem and petiole of a leaf.
steps: Collenchyma: living, corner-thickened → support to growing parts
solution.why_others_wrong: Seed coats of legumes and fruit walls of nuts are sites of sclereids. Old wood is not supported by collenchyma.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Collenchyma)
solution.final_answer: Option A: growing parts of the plant, such as the young stem and the petiole of a leaf

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Except for the main veins, the vascular bundles of an isobilateral (monocot) leaf are of nearly similar size.
Reason (R): Monocot leaves have parallel venation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT explains that the parallel venation in monocot leaves is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles (except in main veins), whereas in dicot leaves the veins vary in thickness. R explains A.
steps: Parallel venation → bundles of similar size → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Monocotyledonous (Isobilateral) Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (part of a dicot stem) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Pericycle
B. Medullary rays
C. Pith
D. Epidermis

List-II:
I. A few layers of radially placed parenchymatous cells between the vascular bundles
II. Covered with a thin cuticle; may bear trichomes and a few stomata
III. Semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma above the phloem
IV. Rounded parenchymatous cells with large intercellular spaces in the central portion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Internal structure of a dicot stem
solution.explanation: In a dicot stem the epidermis is covered with a thin cuticle and may bear trichomes and a few stomata. The pericycle lies on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem as semi-lunar patches of sclerenchyma. Radially placed parenchyma cells between bundles form medullary rays. The central pith has rounded parenchyma cells with large intercellular spaces.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Dicotyledonous Stem
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about simple permanent tissues are correct?

(a) Parenchyma cells may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated in shape.
(b) Collenchyma cells often contain chloroplasts.
(c) Intercellular spaces are absent in collenchyma.
(d) Sclereids have very wide cavities (lumen).
(e) Collenchyma is found in layers below the epidermis in monocotyledonous plants.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Parenchyma cells are generally isodiametric but may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated. Collenchyma cells often contain chloroplasts and have no intercellular spaces; the tissue lies below the epidermis in dicotyledonous plants. Sclereids are highly thickened dead cells with very narrow cavities.
steps: (d) false: the lumen is very narrow
(e) false: collenchyma is described below the epidermis in dicots
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Permanent tissues)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Subsidiary cells are the two bean-shaped cells that directly enclose the stomatal pore.
Statement II: Epidermal cells are parenchymatous, with a large amount of cytoplasm and a small vacuole.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Each stoma has two bean-shaped guard cells enclosing the pore; subsidiary cells are specialised epidermal cells in the vicinity of the guard cells. Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole.
steps: Statement I: false, these are the guard cells
Statement II: false, a small amount of cytoplasm and a large vacuole
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (Epidermal tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about phloem are correct?

(a) The end walls of sieve tube elements are perforated in a sieve-like manner to form sieve plates.
(b) Phloem fibres have pointed, needle-like apices.
(c) The walls of phloem parenchyma cells have pits through which plasmodesmatal connections exist between cells.
(d) Phloem fibres remain living at maturity.
(e) A mature sieve element possesses a peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Sieve tube elements have sieve plates in their end walls; a mature element has peripheral cytoplasm and a large vacuole but no nucleus. Phloem parenchyma has cellulose walls with pits carrying plasmodesmatal connections. Phloem fibres are elongated with needle-like apices and, at maturity, lose their protoplasm and become dead.
steps: (d) false: phloem fibres become dead at maturity
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Phloem)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The vascular bundles of a monocot stem are described as closed.
Reason (R): In a monocot stem, the peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Vascular bundles are closed when there is no cambium between xylem and phloem, as in monocots. The smaller size of the peripheral bundles is a true but separate feature; it does not explain why the bundles are closed.
steps: Bundle size has nothing to do with the absence of cambium
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Monocotyledonous Stem; The Tissue System (Vascular tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (tissue or cell) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Xylem parenchyma
B. Phloem parenchyma
C. Companion cells
D. Spongy parenchyma

List-II:
I. Help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
II. Stores food materials and substances such as resins, latex and mucilage
III. Stores food as starch or fat, and substances such as tannins
IV. Oval or round, loosely arranged cells with large air cavities, extending to the lower epidermis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Living cells of vascular and ground tissues
solution.explanation: Xylem parenchyma stores food as starch or fat and substances like tannins. Phloem parenchyma stores food and substances like resins, latex and mucilage. Companion cells help maintain the pressure gradient in sieve tubes. Spongy parenchyma in a dorsiventral leaf has loosely arranged oval or round cells with large spaces and air cavities.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tannins are linked with xylem parenchyma, and resins, latex and mucilage with phloem parenchyma; the options that swap them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Xylem; Phloem); Dicotyledonous (Dorsiventral) Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the anatomy of roots, stems and leaves are correct?

(a) Both dicot and monocot roots have an endodermis and a pericycle.
(b) A monocot stem has a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue.
(c) Monocot roots do not undergo any secondary growth.
(d) In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thin-walled bundle sheath cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Monocot roots, like dicot roots, have epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, and they do not undergo any secondary growth. A monocot stem has scattered bundles in a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells.
steps: (d) false: the bundle sheath cells are thick-walled
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Medullary rays are a part of the vascular tissue system.
Statement II: In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled, chloroplast-containing cells called mesophyll.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. In primary stems and roots it includes the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays. In leaves, the ground tissue is the mesophyll.
steps: Statement I: false, medullary rays belong to the ground tissue system
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (Ground tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Who first saw and described a live cell?

solution.explanation: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus.
steps: First live cell seen and described → Leeuwenhoek
solution.why_others_wrong: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus. Schleiden contributed to the cell theory. Virchow explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', What is a Cell?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In green plants, the majority of the chloroplasts are found in the:

solution.explanation: The majority of the chloroplasts of green plants are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves. They are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like organelles.
solution.why_others_wrong: Root cells and root caps are not the main photosynthetic cells, and vessels are dead conducting elements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option A: mesophyll cells of the leaves

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a prokaryotic cell, several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain. This chain is called a:

solution.explanation: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or a polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
steps: Many ribosomes on one mRNA → polysome
solution.why_others_wrong: A mesosome is an infolding of the plasma membrane, the nucleoid is the naked genomic DNA region and a plasmid is a small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (Ribosomes and inclusion bodies)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A single human cell contains a thread of DNA, distributed among its 46 chromosomes, that is approximately:

solution.concept: Length of DNA in a human cell
solution.explanation: A single human cell has approximately two metre long thread of DNA distributed among its 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).
steps: Human cell: about 2 m of DNA in 46 chromosomes
solution.why_others_wrong: The other lengths are not the NCERT value; they differ by factors of a thousand or more, or by ten.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell) with List-II (shape).

List-I:
A. Red blood cell
B. White blood cell
C. Mesophyll cell
D. Nerve cell

List-II:
I. Round and oval
II. Branched and long
III. Round and biconcave
IV. Amoeboid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cells vary greatly in shape. In the NCERT figure, red blood cells are round and biconcave, white blood cells amoeboid, mesophyll cells round and oval, and nerve cells branched and long.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', An Overview of Cell (Figure: different shapes of cells)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Matthias Schleiden, who examined a large number of plants, was a British zoologist.
Statement II: Theodore Schwann reported that cells have a thin outer layer, known today as the plasma membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Matthias Schleiden (1838) was a German botanist, and Theodore Schwann (1839) a British zoologist. Schwann reported that cells have a thin outer layer, today known as the plasma membrane, and concluded that the cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.
steps: Statement I: false, Schleiden was a German botanist
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Theory
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).
