questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The dough used for making foods such as dosa and idli is fermented by bacteria. Its puffed-up appearance is due to the production of:

solution.explanation: NCERT notes that the dough used for making dosa and idli is fermented by bacteria. The puffed-up appearance of the dough is due to the production of CO₂ gas.
steps: Bacterial fermentation of dough → CO₂ → puffed-up dough
solution.why_others_wrong: Fermentation releases CO₂, not oxygen. Methane and hydrogen sulphide are produced by anaerobic bacteria in sludge digesters and biogas plants, not in dough.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in household products

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, but its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by:

solution.explanation: Fleming found that a chemical produced by the mould Penicillium notatum inhibited Staphylococci, and named it penicillin. Its full potential as an effective antibiotic was established much later by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey. Penicillin was extensively used to treat American soldiers wounded in World War II, and Fleming, Chain and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945.
steps: Full potential established: Chain and Florey
solution.why_others_wrong: The other pairs are known for different work (germ theory, the lac operon, recombinant DNA) and did not develop penicillin.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products: antibiotics
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ernest Chain and Howard Florey

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Azospirillum and Azotobacter are used as biofertilisers because they:

options.text: Fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil
Fix nitrogen only inside root nodules of leguminous plants
Are fungi that form mycorrhiza and absorb phosphorus for the plant
Are cyanobacteria that add organic matter to paddy fields

solution.explanation: Biofertilisers are organisms that enrich the nutrient quality of the soil; the main sources are bacteria, fungi and cyanobacteria. Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in root nodules of legumes, while other bacteria such as Azospirillum and Azotobacter can fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil, enriching its nitrogen content.
solution.why_others_wrong: Root-nodule fixation is done by Rhizobium. Mycorrhizal fungi (e.g. Glomus) absorb phosphorus. Azospirillum and Azotobacter are bacteria, not cyanobacteria.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option A: Fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: BOD refers to the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria.
Statement II: The greater the BOD of waste water, the lower is its polluting potential.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: BOD is the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria. It is an indirect measure of the organic matter present, so the greater the BOD of waste water, the more is its polluting potential. Sewage is treated until its BOD is reduced.
steps: Statement II: false, higher BOD means higher polluting potential
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment: secondary treatment
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term in sewage treatment) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Flocs
B. Primary sludge
C. Gas produced in anaerobic sludge digesters
D. Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan

List-II:
I. Initiated by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to save major rivers from water pollution
II. Masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments that form mesh-like structures
III. A mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon dioxide
IV. All the solids that settle during primary treatment

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In primary treatment, all the solids that settle form the primary sludge. In secondary treatment, aerobic microbes grow into flocs, masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments forming mesh-like structures. In anaerobic sludge digesters, bacteria digest the sludge and produce a mixture of gases such as methane, H₂S and CO₂ (biogas). The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save these major rivers from pollution.
steps: Action Plans → Ministry of Environment and Forests (D-I)
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap flocs with primary sludge, the digester gases with the Action Plans, or primary sludge with the digester gases.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough, diphtheria and leprosy.
Reason (R): Antibiotics are chemical substances produced by some microbes that can kill or retard the growth of other (disease-causing) microbes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Antibiotics, produced by some microbes, kill or retard the growth of disease-causing microbes. Because they act on the pathogens themselves, they have greatly improved our capacity to treat deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu) and leprosy (kusht rog). R explains A.
steps: Killing or inhibiting the pathogens is why these diseases became treatable → A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products: antibiotics
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Bread dough is fermented using baker's yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
(b) Lactic acid bacteria in our stomach play a beneficial role in checking disease-causing microbes.
(c) A biogas plant has a concrete tank, 10–15 feet deep, fed with a slurry of dung, and a floating cover that keeps rising as gas is produced.
(d) Fleming discovered penicillin while working on Streptococcus bacteria.
(e) Microbial products are produced on an industrial scale in very small vessels called fermentors.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Microbes in household products, industry and biogas
solution.explanation: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) ferments bread dough. Lactic acid bacteria in our stomach help check disease-causing microbes. A biogas plant has a 10–15 feet deep concrete tank fed with dung slurry, with a floating cover that rises as the gas is produced. Fleming was working on Staphylococci when he noticed the Penicillium mould. Industrial production needs very large vessels called fermentors.
steps: (d) False: he was working on Staphylococci
(e) False: fermentors are very large vessels
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e), or leave out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', household products; industrial products; microbes in production of biogas

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The use of biocontrol measures will greatly reduce our dependence on toxic chemicals and pesticides.
Reason (R): Biocontrol refers to the use of chemical methods for controlling plant diseases and pests.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests, for example ladybirds against aphids, dragonflies against mosquitoes, Bacillus thuringiensis against caterpillars and Trichoderma against plant pathogens. Using such measures greatly reduces dependence on toxic chemicals and pesticides. A is true; R is false because biocontrol uses biological, not chemical, methods.
steps: R: false, biocontrol uses biological methods
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Once the BOD of the waste water is reduced significantly in the aeration tanks, the effluent is passed into a settling tank where the bacterial flocs are allowed to sediment; this sediment is called activated sludge.
Statement II: In anaerobic sludge digesters, bacteria that grow aerobically digest the bacteria and fungi present in the sludge.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: After the BOD is reduced, the effluent goes to a settling tank where the flocs sediment as activated sludge. A small part of it is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum, and the major part goes to large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. There, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge and release gases such as methane, H₂S and CO₂.
steps: Statement II: false, the digester bacteria grow anaerobically
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment: secondary treatment
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: An age pyramid that is urn-shaped, with a narrow base of pre-reproductive individuals, represents a population that is:

solution.explanation: Plotting the age distribution (pre-reproductive, reproductive and post-reproductive individuals) gives an age pyramid. Its shape reflects the growth status of the population: a triangular pyramid with a broad base shows an expanding population, a bell-shaped pyramid a stable population, and an urn-shaped pyramid a declining population.
solution.why_others_wrong: Expanding (and exponentially growing) populations have a broad base; a stable population gives a bell-shaped pyramid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population attributes: age pyramids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The logistic model of population growth, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K], is also called the:

solution.explanation: A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows an initial lag phase, then acceleration and deceleration, and finally an asymptote at the carrying capacity. This type of growth is called Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth and is described by dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K].
solution.why_others_wrong: Gause's principle concerns competition, MacArthur's warblers illustrate resource partitioning, and Humboldt described the species-area relationship.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: growth models

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Cattle egrets always forage close to where cattle are grazing, because the moving cattle stir up and flush out insects that the egrets would otherwise find hard to catch. The cattle are not affected. This association is an example of:

solution.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. NCERT describes the cattle egret and grazing cattle as a classic example: the egret benefits by catching the insects flushed out by the cattle, and the cattle are unaffected.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mutualism needs both to benefit; parasitism harms the cattle; amensalism harms one partner and leaves the other unaffected.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: commensalism

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Absolute population numbers are not always needed. To find out whether the fish population of a lake has changed, NCERT suggests that a good enough measure of its population density is:

options.text: The total number of fish species in the lake
The number of fish caught per trap
The percent cover of aquatic plants

solution.explanation: Total number is generally the most appropriate measure of population density, but it is sometimes hard to obtain or not needed. If we only want to know whether a population is growing or declining, relative density serves well: the number of fish caught per trap is a good enough measure of the total fish population density in a lake.
steps: Relative density can replace absolute numbers
Fish in a lake → number caught per trap
solution.why_others_wrong: The number of species measures diversity, not density of one population. Plant cover and phytoplankton biomass do not measure the fish population.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population attributes: population density
solution.final_answer: Option B: The number of fish caught per trap

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Chemicals such as nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium are produced by plants as defences against grazers and browsers.
Statement II: In the association between the clown fish and the sea anemone, the sea anemone benefits by hosting the clown fish.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Plants produce many chemicals, such as nicotine, caffeine, quinine, strychnine and opium, as defences against grazers and browsers. The clown fish living among the stinging tentacles of a sea anemone gets protection from predators, but the anemone does not appear to derive any benefit: this is commensalism.
steps: Statement II: false, the anemone does not appear to benefit
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation and commensalism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a population growing exponentially, the per capita birth rate is 0.30 and the per capita death rate is 0.18 per individual per year. Using dN/dt = (b − d)N, what is the rate of increase of the population when it has 1000 individuals?

solution.explanation: In exponential growth, dN/dt = (b − d) × N, where (b − d) = r, the intrinsic rate of natural increase. r = 0.30 − 0.18 = 0.12 per individual per year, so dN/dt = 0.12 × 1000 = 120 individuals per year.
solution.why_others_wrong: 480 adds the death rate instead of subtracting it. 300 ignores deaths. 0.12 is r itself, not multiplied by N.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are features of parasites, as described by NCERT?

(a) Loss of unnecessary sense organs.
(b) Presence of adhesive organs or suckers to cling on to the host.
(c) Loss of the digestive system.
(d) Low reproductive capacity.
(e) Many parasites are host-specific, so that the host and the parasite tend to co-evolve.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Many parasites have evolved to be host-specific, so that host and parasite tend to co-evolve. In accordance with their life styles, parasites show special adaptations: loss of unnecessary sense organs, presence of adhesive organs or suckers to cling on to the host, loss of the digestive system and high reproductive capacity.
steps: (d) False: they have high reproductive capacity
solution.why_others_wrong: Option A leaves out the true statement (e); options B and C include the false statement (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: parasitism

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (pair of organisms) with List-II (interaction).

List-I:
A. Flamingoes and resident fishes in South American lakes
B. Tiger and deer
C. Ticks and dog
D. Barnacles growing on the back of a whale

List-II:
I. Commensalism
II. Competition
III. Parasitism
IV. Predation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Flamingoes and resident fishes in some shallow South American lakes compete for their common food, the zooplankton. A tiger eating a deer is predation. Ticks on dogs are ectoparasites. Barnacles growing on the back of a whale benefit while the whale derives no noticeable benefit: commensalism.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap competition with predation, parasitism with commensalism, or competition with commensalism.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a broad ecological context, herbivores are not very different from predators.
Reason (R): Biological control methods adopted in agricultural pest control are based on the ability of the predator to regulate the prey population.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements come from NCERT's account of predation. A says herbivores, which eat plants, behave like predators in an ecological sense. R describes the use of predators in biological pest control. The basis of biological control does not explain why herbivores resemble predators, so R is not the explanation of A.
steps: R is about biological pest control, not about herbivores → B
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In 1981, the intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) for the human population in India was 0.0205.
Statement II: The r values given by NCERT for the Norway rat and the flour beetle are 0.015 and 0.12 respectively.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In dN/dt = rN, r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase, an important parameter for assessing the impact of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth. NCERT gives r = 0.015 for the Norway rat and 0.12 for the flour beetle; in 1981, r for the human population in India was 0.0205.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: exponential growth
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When all the starfish Pisaster were removed from an enclosed intertidal area of the American Pacific Coast, more than 10 species of invertebrates became extinct within a year.
Reason (R): In the absence of the predator, interspecific competition among the prey species increased.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Role of predators in maintaining diversity
solution.explanation: In the rocky intertidal communities of the American Pacific Coast, Pisaster is an important predator. When it was removed experimentally, more than 10 invertebrate species became extinct within a year because of interspecific competition. Predators reduce the intensity of competition among prey; without them, superior competitors eliminate others. R explains A.
steps: Loss of predator → stronger competition → extinctions → A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population interactions: predation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about population growth are correct?

(a) Exponential growth can be written in integral form as Nₜ = N₀e^(rt), where e is the base of natural logarithms (2.71828).
(b) Population density depends on four basic processes, of which natality and immigration increase it.
(c) Under normal conditions, births and deaths are the most important factors influencing population density.
(d) When resources in the habitat are unlimited, a population grows in a logistic fashion.
(e) In nature, a habitat has unlimited resources and supports exponential growth indefinitely.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Population density changes through natality and immigration (which increase it) and mortality and emigration (which decrease it); normally births and deaths matter most. With unlimited resources a population grows exponentially, Nₜ = N₀e^(rt). In nature resources are finite, so no population can grow exponentially indefinitely; growth is logistic and levels off at the carrying capacity.
steps: (d) False: unlimited resources give exponential growth
(e) False: resources in nature are finite
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and D include (d) or (e), or leave out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Under normal conditions, births and deaths are the most important factors influencing population density. When a new habitat is just being colonised, however, which factor may contribute more significantly to population growth than birth rates?

solution.explanation: Of the four processes that change population density, natality and mortality are the most important under normal conditions. Immigration and emigration assume importance only under special conditions: for instance, when a new habitat is just being colonised, immigration may contribute more significantly to population growth than birth rates.
steps: Normal conditions → births and deaths dominate
Newly colonised habitat → immigration may dominate
solution.why_others_wrong: Natality is the birth rate itself, which the question compares against. Mortality and emigration decrease population density.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A population growing exponentially gives a J-shaped curve when its size N is plotted against time.
Reason (R): In exponential growth, the per capita growth rate decreases as the population size N approaches the carrying capacity K.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: With unlimited resources, a population grows exponentially (dN/dt = rN) and a plot of N against time gives a J-shaped curve; the per capita growth rate r stays constant. A growth rate that slows as N approaches the carrying capacity K is the feature of logistic growth, dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. A is true; R is false.
steps: R: false, slowing near K is a feature of logistic growth; r is constant in exponential growth
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Organisms and Populations', population growth: growth models
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The identification and enumeration of the plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its:

solution.explanation: The interaction of biotic and abiotic components results in a physical structure characteristic of each type of ecosystem. Identification and enumeration of the plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its species composition; the vertical distribution of species at different levels is called stratification.
steps: Listing and counting species → species composition
solution.why_others_wrong: Stratification is the vertical layering of species. Standing crop is the living mass at a trophic level. NPP is a rate of biomass production; none of these is obtained by listing species.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The biomass of a species at a trophic level can be expressed in terms of fresh weight or dry weight. According to NCERT, which of these is the more accurate measure?

options.text: Neither; biomass can only be expressed as number of individuals

solution.explanation: The standing crop of a trophic level is measured as the biomass of living organisms or as their number in a unit area. Biomass is expressed as fresh or dry weight; measurement in terms of dry weight is more accurate.
solution.why_others_wrong: Fresh weight varies with the water content of the organisms, which is why NCERT calls dry weight the more accurate measure; biomass is not limited to counts of individuals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow: standing crop and biomass

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an aquatic ecosystem?

solution.explanation: Ecosystems are broadly terrestrial or aquatic. Forest, grassland and desert are terrestrial ecosystems; pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are aquatic ecosystems. Crop fields and an aquarium may be considered man-made ecosystems.
steps: Aquatic: pond, lake, wetland, river, estuary
solution.why_others_wrong: Forest, grassland and desert are the terrestrial examples given by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a terrestrial ecosystem, the major producers are herbaceous and woody plants.
Statement II: All organisms in an ecosystem depend for their food on producers, either directly or indirectly.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Producers are autotrophs that fix solar energy into food. In terrestrial ecosystems the major producers are herbaceous and woody plants; in aquatic ecosystems they are phytoplankton, algae and higher plants. All organisms depend on producers for food, directly (herbivores) or indirectly (carnivores and decomposers).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The gross primary productivity of a grassland is 25,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹, and the producers use 40 per cent of it in respiration. What is the net primary productivity of the grassland?

solution.explanation: Net primary productivity is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R) of the producers: NPP = GPP − R. R = 40% of 25,000 = 10,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹, so NPP = 25,000 − 10,000 = 15,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹. NPP is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs.
steps: NPP = GPP − R = 15,000 kJ m⁻² yr⁻¹
solution.why_others_wrong: 10,000 is the respiratory loss, not NPP. 35,000 adds respiration instead of subtracting it. 2,500 wrongly applies the 10 per cent law, which concerns transfer between trophic levels.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (component of a pond ecosystem) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Abiotic component
B. Autotrophs
C. Consumers
D. Decomposers

List-II:
I. Fungi, bacteria and flagellates, especially abundant at the bottom of the pond
II. Water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances, and the rich soil deposit at the bottom
III. Convert inorganic material into organic material with the help of the radiant energy of the sun
IV. Zooplankton, and free-swimming and bottom-dwelling animals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A pond is a shallow water body in which all the basic components of an ecosystem are well exhibited. The abiotic component is the water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom. Autotrophs (phytoplankton, some algae and floating, submerged and marginal plants) convert inorganic into organic material using solar energy. Consumers are zooplankton and free-swimming and bottom forms. Decomposers are fungi, bacteria and flagellates, especially abundant at the bottom.
steps: Abiotic → water, dissolved substances, soil deposit (A-II)
Autotrophs → solar energy to organic matter (B-III)
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the abiotic component with the autotrophs, the consumers with the decomposers, or the autotrophs with the consumers.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function (pond)
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Humus serves as a reservoir of nutrients.
Reason (R): Humus is colloidal in nature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Humification leads to the accumulation of humus, a dark-coloured amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes at an extremely slow rate. NCERT states that, being colloidal in nature, it serves as a reservoir of nutrients. R gives the reason for A.
steps: NCERT: 'being colloidal in nature it serves as a reservoir of nutrients' → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', decomposition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about trophic levels are correct?

(a) A trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such.
(b) Herbivores are primary consumers; the consumers that feed on herbivores are primary carnivores (secondary consumers).
(c) The standing crop of a trophic level is measured as the biomass of living organisms or their number in a unit area.
(d) The number of trophic levels in a grazing food chain is unlimited.
(e) Primary carnivores are also called primary consumers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Organisms occupy a place in the food chain called the trophic level. A trophic level is a functional level, not a species. Herbivores are primary consumers; animals eating them are primary carnivores, i.e. secondary consumers. The standing crop is measured as biomass or number per unit area. Because only about 10% of energy passes to the next level, the number of trophic levels in a grazing food chain is restricted.
steps: (d) False: the number of trophic levels is restricted
(e) False: primary carnivores are secondary consumers
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e), or leave out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow; ecological pyramids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In ecological pyramids, the base is always formed by the producers and the apex by the top-level consumers.
Statement II: Ecological pyramids take into account a species that belongs to two or more trophic levels.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The base of each pyramid represents the producers (first trophic level) and the apex the tertiary or top-level consumers. Among the limitations of ecological pyramids, NCERT notes that they do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.
steps: Statement II: false, this is a limitation of ecological pyramids
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The pyramid of numbers in a grassland ecosystem is upright.
Reason (R): In a grassland, the producers (about 58 lakh in NCERT's example) far outnumber the herbivores, which in turn far outnumber the carnivores.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Pyramid of numbers in a grassland
solution.explanation: In NCERT's grassland pyramid of numbers, about 58 lakh producers support far fewer primary consumers, still fewer secondary consumers and only a handful of tertiary consumers. Because the number of individuals falls steeply at each higher trophic level, the pyramid is broad at the base and narrow at the top, i.e. upright. R explains A.
steps: Numbers shrink upward → upright pyramid → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecological pyramids: pyramid of numbers
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about productivity are correct?

(a) Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.
(b) A considerable amount of gross primary productivity is utilised by plants in respiration.
(c) Net primary productivity is the biomass available for consumption by heterotrophs, i.e. herbivores and decomposers.
(d) Net primary productivity is the energy fixed by the consumers per unit time.
(e) The amount of biomass produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis is called the standing crop.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Primary production is the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. GPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis; a considerable part of it is used in plant respiration. GPP minus respiration losses is NPP, the biomass available to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers). The standing crop is the living mass present at a trophic level at a given time.
steps: (d) False: NPP refers to producers, not consumers
(e) False: that is primary production, not standing crop
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e), or leave out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', productivity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A person eats rice and also eats a fish. The fish fed on zooplankton, which fed on phytoplankton. In these two food chains, the person occupies the trophic levels of:

options.text: Primary consumer and tertiary consumer at the same time
Primary consumer and secondary consumer at the same time

solution.explanation: Rice is a producer, so in the chain rice → person the person is a primary consumer. In the chain phytoplankton → zooplankton → fish → person, the person is a tertiary consumer (fourth trophic level). A given species may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time.
steps: Phytoplankton → zooplankton → fish → person: tertiary consumer
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Only' options ignore one of the two chains. The fish is the secondary consumer, so the person eating it is tertiary, not secondary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', energy flow; ecological pyramids
solution.final_answer: Option B: Primary consumer and tertiary consumer at the same time

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a pond, the decomposition and mineralisation of dead organic matter release nutrients back for reuse by the autotrophs.
Statement II: In a pond, the radiant energy of the sun is converted into chemical energy when the heterotrophs consume the autotrophs.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: A pond performs all the functions of an ecosystem: autotrophs convert inorganic into organic material using the radiant energy of the sun; heterotrophs consume the autotrophs; and dead organic matter is decomposed and mineralised to release nutrients for reuse by the autotrophs. Energy moves in one direction towards the higher trophic levels and is lost as heat. Conversion of radiant energy is done by the autotrophs, not by the heterotrophs.
steps: Statement II: false, autotrophs convert solar energy; heterotrophs only consume them
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Ecosystem', ecosystem: structure and function (pond)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The four major causes of the accelerated loss of biodiversity, namely habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions, are together described as:

solution.explanation: NCERT names four major causes of the accelerated rates of species extinctions: habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions. Together they are called 'The Evil Quartet'.
solution.why_others_wrong: The sixth extinction is the present episode of mass extinction. The rivet popper hypothesis (Paul Ehrlich) is an analogy for species in ecosystems. The species-area relationship describes how species richness varies with area.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity: causes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to the ethical argument for conserving biodiversity, besides realising that every species has an intrinsic value, NCERT says that we have a moral duty to:

options.text: Conserve only those species that are of current economic value to us
Care for the well-being of all species and pass on our biological legacy in good order to future generations
Explore molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance
Protect only the species that provide ecosystem services such as pollination

solution.explanation: The ethical argument relates to what we owe to the millions of plant, animal and microbe species with whom we share this planet. Every species has an intrinsic value, even if it may not be of current economic value to us, and we have a moral duty to care for their well-being and pass on our biological legacy in good order to future generations.
steps: Ethical argument: intrinsic value of every species → moral duty to care for all species and hand on the biological legacy
solution.why_others_wrong: Conserving only economically useful species contradicts the ethical argument. Exploring diversity for products of economic importance is bioprospecting (narrowly utilitarian). Ecosystem services such as pollination belong to the broadly utilitarian argument.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: why should we conserve biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option B: Care for the well-being of all species and pass on our biological legacy in good order to future generations

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Among recent extinctions, NCERT lists three subspecies of tiger. They are:

solution.explanation: Examples of recent extinctions given by NCERT include the dodo (Mauritius), quagga (Africa), thylacine (Australia), Steller's sea cow (Russia) and three subspecies of tiger: Bali, Javan and Caspian.
steps: Extinct tiger subspecies: Bali, Javan, Caspian
solution.why_others_wrong: The Bengal, Siberian and Sumatran tigers are not among the extinct subspecies listed by NCERT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option D: Bali, Javan and Caspian

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Greenland, at 71° N, has only 56 species of birds, whereas New York, at 41° N, has 105 species.
Statement II: India, with much of its land area in the tropical latitudes, has more than 1,200 species of birds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Species diversity generally decreases from the equator towards the poles. NCERT's bird example: Colombia near the equator has nearly 1,400 species, New York (41° N) 105 species and Greenland (71° N) only 56 species. India, with much of its land area in the tropical latitudes, has more than 1,200 species of birds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: latitudinal gradients
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about global species diversity are correct?

(a) The number of fungi species in the world is more than the combined total of the species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals.
(b) Global estimates of species diversity do not give any figures for prokaryotes.
(c) Conventional taxonomic methods are not suitable for identifying microbial species, and many species are simply not culturable under laboratory conditions.
(d) The diversity of prokaryotes has been fully documented.
(e) The total number of species described so far is slightly more than 15 million.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: According to the IUCN (2004), slightly more than 1.5 million plant and animal species have been described so far. The number of fungi species exceeds the combined species of fishes, amphibians, reptiles and mammals. Estimates give no figures for prokaryotes, because conventional taxonomic methods do not suit microbes and many are not culturable in the laboratory; their diversity could run into millions.
steps: (d) False: prokaryote diversity is not known
(e) False: about 1.5 million species have been described
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (d) or (e), or leave out (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity: how many species are there on earth

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group in the Amazonian rain forest) with List-II (approximate number of species given by NCERT).

List-I:
A. Plants
B. Fishes
C. Birds
D. Invertebrates

List-II:
I. 1,300
II. More than 1,25,000
III. 40,000
IV. 3,000

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The largely tropical Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest biodiversity on earth. NCERT notes that it is home to more than 40,000 species of plants, 3,000 of fishes, 1,300 of birds, 427 of mammals, 427 of amphibians, 378 of reptiles and more than 1,25,000 invertebrates.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap plants with invertebrates, fishes with birds, or birds with invertebrates.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: latitudinal gradients
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Tropical rain forests, which once covered more than 14 per cent of the earth's land surface, now cover no more than 6 per cent.
Reason (R): Many marine fish populations around the world are over-harvested, endangering the continued existence of some commercially important species.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements are NCERT examples of causes of biodiversity loss. A is an example of habitat loss: tropical rain forests have shrunk from over 14% to no more than 6% of the land surface. R is an example of over-exploitation of marine fish. Over-harvesting of fish does not explain the shrinking of rain forests, so R is not the explanation of A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity: causes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ecologists believe that communities with more species generally tend to be more stable than those with fewer species.
Statement II: A stable community should show a great deal of variation in productivity from year to year.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Ecologists believe that communities with more species tend to be more stable. A stable community should not show too much variation in productivity from year to year; it must be either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbances (natural or man-made) and resistant to invasions by alien species.
steps: Statement II: false, a stable community shows little year-to-year variation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity and ecosystem stability
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (group) with List-II (percentage of its species facing the threat of extinction, as given by NCERT).

List-I:
A. Birds
B. Mammals
C. Amphibians
D. Gymnosperms

List-II:
I. 12 per cent
II. 23 per cent
III. 32 per cent
IV. 31 per cent

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: More than 15,500 species world-wide are facing the threat of extinction. NCERT gives the present figures: 12 per cent of all bird species, 23 per cent of all mammal species, 32 per cent of all amphibian species and 31 per cent of all gymnosperm species in the world face the threat of extinction.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap birds with mammals, amphibians with gymnosperms, or mammals with amphibians.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the effects of biodiversity loss and ecosystem stability are correct?

(a) Loss of biodiversity in a region may lead to a decline in plant production.
(b) Loss of biodiversity in a region increases the resistance of the ecosystem to environmental perturbations such as drought.
(c) Loss of biodiversity may increase the variability in certain ecosystem processes such as plant productivity, water use, and pest and disease cycles.
(d) Loss of biodiversity does not affect any ecosystem process.
(e) A stable community is either resistant or resilient to occasional disturbance and is resistant to invasions by alien species.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT states that loss of biodiversity in a region may lead to (a) a decline in plant production, (b) lowered resistance to environmental perturbations such as drought, and (c) increased variability in certain ecosystem processes such as plant productivity, water use, and pest and disease cycles. A stable community is resistant or resilient to occasional disturbance and resistant to invasions by alien species.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options A, B and C include (b) or (d).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', loss of biodiversity; biodiversity and ecosystem stability

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: More solar energy is available in the tropics, which contributes to higher productivity and might, in turn, contribute indirectly to greater diversity.
Statement II: Unlike the tropics, temperate regions have remained relatively undisturbed by glaciations for millions of years, giving them a long evolutionary time for species diversification.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Why the tropics are more diverse
solution.explanation: NCERT gives several hypotheses: speciation is generally a function of time, and unlike temperate regions, which were subjected to frequent glaciations in the past, tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, giving a long evolutionary time for diversification; tropical environments are less seasonal and more predictable; and more solar energy in the tropics gives higher productivity, which might indirectly contribute to greater diversity. Statement II reverses the roles of the tropical and temperate regions.
steps: Statement II: false, it is the tropics that remained undisturbed; temperate regions faced frequent glaciations
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', patterns of biodiversity: latitudinal gradients
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

D. Species world-wide currently facing the threat of extinction

List-II:
I. 87
II. More than 15,500
III. 359

solution.explanation: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species in the last 500 years: 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants. More than 15,500 species world-wide currently face the threat of extinction.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Strict protection of the biodiversity hotspots could reduce the ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30 per cent.
Reason (R): Biodiversity hotspots are regions with low species richness but a very high degree of endemism.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Hotspots are regions with very high levels of species richness and a high degree of endemism. Although all the hotspots together cover less than 2 per cent of the earth's land area, they harbour so many species that their strict protection could reduce the ongoing mass extinctions by almost 30 per cent. A is true; R is false because hotspots have very high, not low, species richness.
steps: R: false, hotspots have very high species richness and high endemism
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Biodiversity and Conservation', biodiversity conservation: hotspots
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In which of the following groups are cells performing the same function arranged into tissues, without tissues being grouped into organs (tissue level of organisation)?

solution.explanation: NCERT: in sponges the cells are loose aggregates (cellular level). In coelenterates the arrangement is more complex: cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues (tissue level). From Platyhelminthes onwards tissues are grouped into organs (organ level), and in annelids, arthropods, molluscs, echinoderms and chordates organs associate to form organ systems (organ-system level).
solution.why_others_wrong: Porifera stop at the cellular level; flatworms form organs; annelids form organ systems.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', basis of classification: levels of organisation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sponges are hermaphrodite: eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual.
Reason (R): Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements about sponges. Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), i.e. eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual. Asexual reproduction is by fragmentation, and sexual reproduction by the formation of gametes. The ability to fragment says nothing about why one individual makes both gametes, so R does not explain A.
steps: R: asexual reproduction by fragmentation → true
Asexual fragmentation is unrelated to the sexual condition → R does not explain A
solution.why_others_wrong: A claims a causal link that does not exist; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Porifera
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about phylum Arthropoda are correct?

(a) Arthropods show the organ-system level of organisation.
(b) The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton.
(c) Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or a tracheal system.
(d) Statocysts are the organs of vision.
(e) Fertilisation is usually external.

solution.explanation: Arthropods are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented, coelomate animals with organ-system level of organisation and a chitinous exoskeleton. Fertilisation is usually internal.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): All chordates are vertebrates.
Reason (R): In vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Members of subphylum Vertebrata possess a notochord during the embryonic period, which is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. Urochordates and cephalochordates are chordates without a vertebral column. Hence all vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates. A is false; R is true.
steps: Urochordata and Cephalochordata lack a vertebral column → A false
Notochord replaced by vertebral column in adult vertebrates → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B treat a false assertion as true; C calls the true reason false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Chordata: subphylum Vertebrata
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the classification of chordates are correct?

(a) Petromyzon and Myxine belong to the division Agnatha.
(b) Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes are placed in the super class Pisces of the division Gnathostomata.
(c) Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves and Mammalia form the super class Tetrapoda.
(d) Cephalochordates possess a vertebral column.
(e) Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum are urochordates.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Vertebrata is divided into Agnatha (lacking jaws; class Cyclostomata, e.g. Petromyzon and Myxine) and Gnathostomata (bearing jaws). Gnathostomata has super class Pisces (Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes) and super class Tetrapoda (Amphibia, Reptilia, Aves, Mammalia). Urochordates (Ascidia, Salpa, Doliolum) and cephalochordates (Branchiostoma) are protochordates without a vertebral column.
steps: (d) False: cephalochordates have a notochord, no vertebral column
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B include the false statement (d); D leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Chordata: classification

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following features is shared by Mollusca and Echinodermata?

options.text: Sexes are usually separate and development is indirect
A water vascular system helps in locomotion and capture of food
A soft spongy mantle covers the visceral hump

solution.explanation: Molluscs are usually dioecious and oviparous with indirect development. In echinoderms, sexes are separate and development is indirect with a free-swimming larva. The water vascular system and adult radial symmetry are echinoderm features; the mantle over the visceral hump is a mollusc feature.
steps: Water vascular system, radial adults → echinoderms only; mantle → molluscs only
solution.why_others_wrong: B and D are found only in echinoderms; C is found only in molluscs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phyla Mollusca and Echinodermata

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate.
Reason (R): Cnidoblasts present on the tentacles and the body of cnidarians are used for anchorage, defence and the capture of prey.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Both are NCERT statements on coelenterates. Cnidarians that form corals have a skeleton of calcium carbonate. Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes), stinging cells on the tentacles and body, serve in anchorage, defence and capture of prey. The stinging cells have nothing to do with the composition of the coral skeleton, so R does not explain A.
steps: A: coral skeleton of CaCO₃ → true
R: cnidoblasts for anchorage, defence, prey capture → true
Stinging cells do not explain skeletal composition → R does not explain A
solution.why_others_wrong: A claims a causal link that does not exist; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Animal Kingdom', phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

Change in the state of matter

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: As a rule of thumb, the rate of a physical or chemical process doubles for every 10 °C rise in temperature (and decreases by half for every 10 °C fall). A non-enzymatic reaction proceeds at a rate R at 20 °C. Assuming the rule holds over this range, its rate at 50 °C will be about:

solution.concept: Effect of temperature on reaction rate
solution.explanation: NCERT: the rate of a physical or chemical process doubles or decreases by half for every 10 °C change in either direction. From 20 °C to 50 °C there are three 10 °C steps, and the rate doubles at each step.
solution.shortcut: Rate factor = 2^(ΔT/10) = 2³ = 8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3R counts the steps instead of doubling; 6R adds a doubling per step (2 × 3); 2.5R simply divides the two temperatures.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: chemical reactions

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In skeletal muscle under anaerobic conditions the pathway from glucose ends in lactic acid, and in yeast during fermentation it leads to ethanol. According to NCERT, glucose is converted into pyruvic acid through:

options.text: About twenty reactions catalysed by ribozymes

solution.explanation: NCERT: glucose → 2 pyruvic acid is a metabolic pathway in which glucose becomes pyruvic acid through ten different enzyme-catalysed metabolic reactions. In skeletal muscle under anaerobic conditions lactic acid is formed; under normal aerobic conditions pyruvic acid is formed; in yeast during fermentation the same pathway leads to ethanol.
steps: Glucose → pyruvic acid: ten enzyme-catalysed reactions
solution.why_others_wrong: The pathway is neither a single reaction nor non-enzymatic, and NCERT does not attribute it to ribozymes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Biomolecules', enzymes: how do enzymes bring about such high rates of chemical conversions?

Supplying the vitamin component of the co-enzyme

questions.subject: Zoology

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Exothermic reactions also pass a transition state → II false

D. Expiration

List-II:
I. Pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture of gases
II. Utilisation of O₂ by the cells for catabolic reactions and resultant release of CO₂
III. Release of the alveolar air out of the body
IV. Drawing in atmospheric air and releasing CO₂-rich alveolar air

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the steps of respiration as breathing or pulmonary ventilation (atmospheric air drawn in and CO₂-rich alveolar air released out), diffusion across the alveolar membrane, transport by blood, diffusion between blood and tissues, and utilisation of O₂ by cells for catabolic reactions with release of CO₂ (cellular respiration). Breathing has two stages: inspiration and expiration (alveolar air released out). The pressure contributed by an individual gas in a mixture is its partial pressure.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap cellular respiration with partial pressure, breathing with expiration, or partial pressure with expiration.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Breathing and Exchange of Gases', respiration: steps; mechanism of breathing; exchange of gases
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the human respiratory system are correct?

(a) Apart from transporting atmospheric air to the alveoli, the conducting part clears it of foreign particles, humidifies it and brings it to body temperature.
(b) The outer pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining, whereas the inner pleural membrane is in contact with the lung surface.
(c) The larynx is the common passage for food and air.
(d) The trachea is a straight tube extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity.
(e) The external nostrils open out below the lower lip.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The conducting part transports air to the alveoli and also clears, humidifies and warms it. The outer pleural membrane lies against the thoracic lining and the inner one against the lung surface. A portion of the pharynx (not the larynx) is the common passage for food and air; the larynx is the sound box. The trachea is a straight tube extending up to the mid-thoracic cavity. The external nostrils open out above the upper lips.
steps: (c) False: the pharynx is the common passage
(e) False: nostrils open above the upper lips
solution.why_others_wrong: A includes (c); B and D include (e) and leave out true statements.

questions.subject: Zoology

Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

Normal rate is 12–16 per minute → II false

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which statement about the oxygen dissociation curve is correct?

It is a straight line, showing that O₂ binding rises evenly with pO₂
It is obtained by plotting pO₂ against the pH of blood
It is a sigmoid curve of the percentage saturation of haemoglobin with O₂ against pO₂, useful in studying the effect of factors like pCO₂ and H⁺ concentration on the binding of O₂ with haemoglobin

solution.explanation: NCERT: a sigmoid curve is obtained when the percentage saturation of haemoglobin with O₂ is plotted against pO₂. This oxygen dissociation curve is highly useful in studying the effect of factors like pCO₂ and H⁺ concentration on the binding of O₂ with haemoglobin.
steps: Axes: pO₂ (x) vs % saturation of Hb with O₂ (y)
Use: effect of pCO₂, H⁺, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The pO₂ in body tissues is higher than that in oxygenated blood.
Reason (R): The pCO₂ in body tissues is about 45 mm Hg.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT's table of partial pressures gives, for tissues, pO₂ 40 mm Hg and pCO₂ 45 mm Hg; for oxygenated blood, pO₂ 95 mm Hg and pCO₂ 40 mm Hg. Tissue pO₂ (40) is lower than that of oxygenated blood (95), which is why O₂ diffuses from blood into tissues. A is false; R is true.
steps: Tissue pO₂ 40 < oxygenated blood pO₂ 95 → A false
Tissue pCO₂ 45 mm Hg → R true
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept a false assertion; C calls the true reason false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the exchange and transport of gases are correct?

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alveoli are the primary sites of gas exchange; exchange also occurs between blood and tissues, by simple diffusion based mainly on pressure or concentration gradients. Haemoglobin is a red, iron-containing pigment in RBCs. Binding of O₂ with haemoglobin is primarily related to the partial pressure of O₂; pCO₂, H⁺ concentration and temperature are other factors that can interfere with it.
steps: (d) False: binding is primarily related to pO₂

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Leucocytes are of two main categories, granulocytes and agranulocytes. Which of the following are agranulocytes?

solution.explanation: NCERT: WBCs are of two main categories: granulocytes (neutrophils, eosinophils and basophils) and agranulocytes (lymphocytes and monocytes).

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood: formed elements

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Plasma is a straw-coloured, viscous fluid. Water constitutes about what proportion of plasma?

solution.explanation: NCERT: plasma constitutes nearly 55 per cent of the blood. 90–92 per cent of plasma is water and proteins contribute 6–8 per cent of it. Formed elements make up nearly 45 per cent of the blood.
solution.why_others_wrong: 55 % is the share of plasma in blood, 45 % that of formed elements, and 6–8 % that of proteins in plasma.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The Rh antigen is observed on the surface of the RBCs of nearly 80 per cent of humans. In a group of 650 people, about how many would be expected to be Rh negative?

solution.explanation: Individuals with the Rh antigen are Rh positive (nearly 80 %); those without it are Rh negative (about 20 %).

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', blood groups: Rh grouping

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular flaps or cusps, the tricuspid valve; the bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle. Semilunar valves guard the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.
solution.why_others_wrong: The mitral and bicuspid valve (the same valve) guards the left side; semilunar valves guard the arterial openings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', human circulatory system: heart

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:

Statement II: Persons with the AB group can accept blood from persons with AB as well as the other groups, so they are called universal recipients.

questions.subject: Zoology

solution.explanation: NCERT: normal activities of the heart are regulated intrinsically (myogenic), but a special neural centre in the medulla oblongata can moderate cardiac function through the autonomic neural system.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology

Match List-I (part of the nodal tissue) with List-II (location or course).

B. Atrio-ventricular node
C. Atrio-ventricular bundle
D. Purkinje fibres

I. Minute fibres spread throughout the ventricular musculature of the respective sides
II. Right upper corner of the right atrium
III. Passes through the atrio-ventricular septa and emerges on the top of the inter-ventricular septum
IV. Lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum

The AV bundle continues from the AVN, passes through the AV septa, emerges on top of the inter-ventricular septum and divides into right and left bundles, which give rise to minute fibres throughout the ventricular musculature: the Purkinje fibres.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the coagulation of blood are correct?

(a) A clot is formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins, in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped.
(b) Thrombokinase is formed by a series of linked enzymic reactions (a cascade process) involving a number of factors present in the plasma in an inactive state.
(c) Certain factors released by the tissues at the site of injury can also initiate coagulation.
(d) The clotting factors are present in the plasma in an active form at all times.
(e) Fibrinogens are plasma proteins needed for the clotting or coagulation of blood.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A clot (coagulum) is mainly a network of fibrin threads trapping dead and damaged formed elements. Fibrins are formed from fibrinogens by thrombin; thrombin forms from prothrombin with the help of thrombokinase, which is formed by a cascade of linked enzymic reactions involving factors present in plasma in an inactive state. Factors released by tissues at the site of injury can also initiate coagulation.
steps: (d) False: the factors are present in an inactive state
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C include the false statement (d); B and C also leave out true statements.

questions.subject: Zoology

Multiple points on the chest only
Both wrists and the right ankle
Each wrist and the left ankle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium.
Statement II: In systemic circulation, deoxygenated blood from the tissues is collected by venules, veins and the vena cava and emptied into the left atrium.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: oxygenated blood from the lungs is carried by the pulmonary veins into the left atrium (Statement I true). Deoxygenated blood from the tissues is collected by venules, veins and the vena cava and emptied into the right atrium (Statement II false).
steps: Pulmonary veins → left atrium → I true
Vena cava → right atrium, not left → II false

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Erythroblastosis foetalis in a second Rh-positive foetus of an Rh-negative mother can be avoided by:

options.text: Giving Rh-positive blood to the mother during her first pregnancy
Administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child
Administering Rh antigens to the foetus before the second delivery
Transfusing group O blood to the mother before the first delivery

solution.explanation: NCERT: the situation (erythroblastosis foetalis) can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.
steps: Prevention → anti-Rh antibodies to the mother
Timing → immediately after the first delivery
solution.why_others_wrong: Exposure to Rh-positive blood or antigens would sensitise rather than protect; ABO group O blood has nothing to do with Rh incompatibility.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In fishes, the heart pumps out deoxygenated blood, which is oxygenated by the gills and supplied to the body parts.
Reason (R): In fishes, oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are received by separate left and right atria and are pumped out by separate ventricles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: fishes have a two-chambered heart with an atrium and a ventricle. The heart pumps out deoxygenated blood, which is oxygenated by the gills and supplied to the body parts, from where deoxygenated blood returns to the heart. Separate left and right atria and ventricles occur in birds and mammals (double circulation), not in fishes. A is true; R is false.
steps: A: fish heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills → true
R: fishes have one atrium and one ventricle → false
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false reason; D calls the true assertion false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about disorders of the circulatory system are correct?

(a) In a normal blood pressure of 120/80 mm Hg, 120 mm Hg is the systolic (pumping) pressure and 80 mm Hg is the diastolic (resting) pressure.
(b) High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and also affects vital organs like the brain and kidney.
(c) Coronary artery disease is often referred to as atherosclerosis.
(d) Angina occurs only in elderly men.
(e) A heart attack is when the heart muscle is suddenly damaged by an inadequate blood supply.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Normal blood pressure is 120/80 mm Hg: 120 is the systolic (pumping) and 80 the diastolic (resting) pressure. High blood pressure leads to heart diseases and also affects the brain and kidney. CAD is often referred to as atherosclerosis. Angina can occur in men and women of any age but is more common among the middle-aged and elderly. A heart attack is sudden damage to heart muscle by an inadequate blood supply.

solution.why_others_wrong: B, C and D include the false statement (d); B and D also leave out true statements.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly pairs an animal group with its pattern of circulation?
