Arthropods: open circulation, in which blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses
Annelids: open circulation, with blood flowing into sinuses
Fishes: double circulation, with separate pulmonary and systemic pathways

solution.explanation: NCERT: the open circulatory system is present in arthropods and molluscs; blood pumped by the heart passes through large vessels into open spaces or body cavities called sinuses. Annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system. Double circulation, with separate pulmonary and systemic pathways, is seen in birds and mammals; fishes have a two-chambered heart.

solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', circulatory pathways

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During the cardiac cycle, atrial systole coincides with ventricular systole.
Statement II: The contraction of the ventricles starts shortly after the Q wave of the ECG and marks the beginning of systole.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Timing of the cardiac cycle and ECG
solution.explanation: NCERT: during ventricular systole the atria undergo relaxation (diastole), so atrial diastole, not atrial systole, coincides with ventricular systole (Statement I false). The QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates ventricular contraction; the contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of systole (Statement II true).
steps: Atrial diastole coincides with ventricular systole → I false
Ventricular contraction begins shortly after Q → II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Body Fluids and Circulation', cardiac cycle; electrocardiograph (ECG)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology

Which of the following statements about the human heart are correct?

(a) The heart is mesodermally derived and is situated in the thoracic cavity between the two lungs, slightly tilted to the left.

A thin muscular wall, the inter-atrial septum, separates the atria, while a thick-walled inter-ventricular septum separates the ventricles. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes mainly excrete their nitrogenous wastes as:

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology

Prevent the formation of renal calculi

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA) is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in the:

options.text: Proximal convoluted tubule and the efferent arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole, at the location of their contact
Collecting duct and the vasa recta
Henle's loop and the peritubular capillaries

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ammonia is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces (in fish) as ammonium ions.
Reason (R): Ammonia is readily soluble.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: ammonia, as it is readily soluble, is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces (in fish) as ammonium ions; kidneys do not play any significant role in its removal. High solubility is why simple diffusion works, so R explains A.
steps: A: ammonia leaves by diffusion across body or gill surfaces → true
R: ammonia is readily soluble → true
NCERT links them with 'as it is readily soluble' → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B denies the link NCERT states; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', introduction: modes of excretion
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (meaning).

List-I:
A. Uremia
B. Micturition reflex
C. Ultrafiltration
D. Renal calculi

List-II:
I. Stone or insoluble mass of crystallised salts (oxalates, etc.) formed within the kidney
II. Accumulation of urea in the blood due to malfunctioning of the kidneys
III. Neural mechanisms causing the release of urine
IV. Glomerular filtration in which almost all the constituents of plasma except proteins pass into Bowman's capsule

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Accumulation of urea in blood is uremia. The neural mechanisms causing release of urine form the micturition reflex. Almost all plasma constituents except proteins pass into Bowman's capsule, so glomerular filtration is considered a process of ultrafiltration. Renal calculi are stones of crystallised salts (oxalates, etc.) formed within the kidney.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap uremia with the micturition reflex, the reflex with ultrafiltration, or ultrafiltration with renal calculi.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation; micturition; disorders of the excretory system
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the regulation of kidney function are correct?

(a) Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration.
(b) Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) is also called vasopressin.
(c) ADH facilitates water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis.
(d) An increase in body fluid volume can switch off the osmoreceptors and suppress ADH release.
(e) A decrease in body fluid volume suppresses ADH release.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Osmoreceptors respond to changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. Excessive loss of fluid activates them, and the hypothalamus releases ADH (vasopressin) from the neurohypophysis. ADH increases water reabsorption from the latter parts of the tubule, preventing diuresis. An increase in body fluid volume switches off the osmoreceptors and suppresses ADH release, completing the feedback. A fall in fluid volume stimulates, not suppresses, ADH release.
steps: (e) False: fluid loss stimulates ADH release
solution.why_others_wrong: A and C include the false statement (e); D leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', regulation of kidney function

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In ureotelic animals, ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver and released into the blood.
Statement II: Some amount of urea may be retained in the kidney matrix of some animals to maintain a desired osmolarity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in ureotelic animals, ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver and released into the blood, which is filtered and excreted by the kidneys. Some amount of urea may be retained in the kidney matrix of some animals to maintain a desired osmolarity. Both statements are true.
steps: Urea made in the liver → I true
Urea retained in kidney matrix for osmolarity → II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', introduction: modes of excretion
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The signal that finally leads to micturition is initiated by:

options.text: The release of ADH from the neurohypophysis
The release of renin by the JG cells
Stretching of the urinary bladder as it fills with urine, which makes stretch receptors on its walls send signals to the CNS

solution.explanation: NCERT: the signal is initiated by the stretching of the urinary bladder as it gets filled with urine. In response, the stretch receptors on the walls of the bladder send signals to the CNS, which passes on motor messages to contract the smooth muscles of the bladder and relax the urethral sphincter, releasing urine.
steps: Bladder fills → stretch receptors → signals to CNS
CNS → bladder muscles contract, urethral sphincter relaxes
solution.why_others_wrong: ADH and renin regulate water and GFR, not micturition; the urethral sphincter relaxes, not contracts, when urine is released.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', micturition
solution.final_answer: Option D: Stretching of the urinary bladder as it fills with urine, which makes stretch receptors on its walls send signals to the CNS

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid in the form of a pellet or paste.
Reason (R): Uric acid, being the least toxic, can be removed with a minimum loss of water.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: ammonia is the most toxic and needs a large amount of water for elimination, whereas uric acid, being the least toxic, can be removed with a minimum loss of water. Uricotelic animals (reptiles, birds, land snails, insects) therefore excrete uric acid as a pellet or paste with a minimum loss of water. R explains A.
steps: A: uric acid as pellet or paste → true
R: least toxic, removable with minimum water → true
Low toxicity allows near-dry excretion → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B denies the link; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', introduction: modes of excretion
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about tubular reabsorption and secretion are correct?

(a) Amino acids and Na⁺ in the filtrate are reabsorbed actively.
(b) Nitrogenous wastes are absorbed by passive transport.
(c) Water is reabsorbed actively in the initial segments of the nephron.
(d) Secretion of H⁺, K⁺ and ammonia into the filtrate helps in the maintenance of the ionic and acid-base balance of body fluids.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the tubular epithelial cells reabsorb by active or passive mechanisms. Substances like glucose, amino acids and Na⁺ are reabsorbed actively, whereas nitrogenous wastes are absorbed by passive transport. Reabsorption of water also occurs passively in the initial segments of the nephron. Tubular cells secrete H⁺, K⁺ and ammonia into the filtrate, which helps maintain the ionic and acid-base balance of body fluids.
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C include the false statement (c); B and C also leave out true statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', urine formation: reabsorption and secretion

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is a function of the distal convoluted tubule (DCT)?

options.text: Reabsorption of nearly all the essential nutrients and 70–80 per cent of electrolytes and water
Reabsorption of HCO₃⁻ and selective secretion of H⁺, K⁺ and NH₃ to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood
Being permeable to water but almost impermeable to electrolytes
Allowing small amounts of urea to pass into the medullary interstitium

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the DCT, conditional reabsorption of Na⁺ and water takes place. The DCT is also capable of reabsorption of HCO₃⁻ and selective secretion of hydrogen and potassium ions and NH₃ to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood.
steps: DCT → HCO₃⁻ reabsorption; H⁺, K⁺, NH₃ secretion
solution.why_others_wrong: A describes the PCT, C the descending limb of Henle's loop and D the collecting duct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option B: Reabsorption of HCO₃⁻ and selective secretion of H⁺, K⁺ and NH₃ to maintain the pH and sodium-potassium balance in blood

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In haemodialysis, the dialysing unit contains a coiled cellophane tube surrounded by dialysing fluid, and nitrogenous wastes move out of the blood across the porous membrane according to the concentration gradient.
Statement II: In the majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the dialysing unit contains a coiled cellophane tube surrounded by dialysing fluid; its porous membrane allows passage of molecules based on concentration gradient, and since nitrogenous wastes are absent in the fluid they move out of the blood (Statement I true). In the majority of nephrons the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla (cortical nephrons); only some, the juxtamedullary nephrons, have very long loops (Statement II false).
steps: Cellophane tube, concentration gradient → I true
Majority are cortical nephrons with short loops → II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', disorders of the excretory system; human excretory system: nephron
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which statement about the collecting duct of the human nephron is correct?

options.text: It is impermeable to water and plays no part in concentrating urine
It lies only in the cortex of the kidney
It receives the filtrate directly from the proximal convoluted tubule
It extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla, and large amounts of water can be reabsorbed from it to produce concentrated urine

solution.explanation: NCERT: the DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called the collecting duct. This long duct extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla. Large amounts of water could be reabsorbed from this region to produce a concentrated urine.
solution.why_others_wrong: The duct reabsorbs much water, runs into the inner medulla, and receives filtrate from the DCT rather than the PCT.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Excretory Products and their Elimination', human excretory system: nephron; function of the tubules
solution.final_answer: Option D: It extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla, and large amounts of water can be reabsorbed from it to produce concentrated urine

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Bone has a very hard matrix because of calcium salts. The matrix of cartilage is slightly pliable because of:

solution.explanation: NCERT: bone has a very hard matrix due to calcium salts, and cartilage has a slightly pliable matrix due to chondroitin salts.
solution.why_others_wrong: Calcium salts make bone hard; collagen alone or sodium chloride is not what NCERT gives.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The human skeletal system consists of a framework of bones and a few cartilages. The total number of bones is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the skeletal system consists of a framework of bones and a few cartilages; it is made up of 206 bones, grouped into the axial skeleton (80 bones) and the appendicular skeleton (126 bones).
solution.why_others_wrong: 80 is the axial and 126 the appendicular skeleton alone; 213 is not an NCERT figure.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it constitutes a:

solution.explanation: NCERT: muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the CNS via a motor neuron. A motor neuron along with the muscle fibres connected to it constitutes a motor unit. The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma is the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
steps: Motor neuron + its muscle fibres → motor unit
solution.why_others_wrong: The motor-end plate is only the junction; a sarcomere is a contractile unit of a myofibril; a myofibril is a fibril within a muscle fibre.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Each clavicle is a long slender bone with two curvatures and is commonly called the collar bone.
Statement II: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet dorsally to form the pubic symphysis, which contains hyaline cartilage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each clavicle is a long slender bone with two curvatures, commonly called the collar bone (Statement I true). The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally to form the pubic symphysis containing fibrous cartilage (Statement II false on two counts).
steps: Clavicle: two curvatures, collar bone → I true
Pubic symphysis: ventral, fibrous cartilage → II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', appendicular skeleton
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Osteoporosis is an age-related disorder with decreased bone mass and increased chances of fractures. A common cause of it is:

options.text: Accumulation of uric acid crystals in the joints
A low level of Ca²⁺ in body fluids
Autoimmune damage at the neuromuscular junction

solution.explanation: NCERT: osteoporosis is an age-related disorder characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chances of fractures. Decreased levels of estrogen is a common cause.
solution.why_others_wrong: Uric acid crystals cause gout; low Ca²⁺ causes tetany; autoimmune damage at the NMJ is myasthenia gravis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', disorders of muscular and skeletal system
solution.final_answer: Option D: Decreased levels of estrogen

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: How many bones in all are present in the wrists, palms and digits of both hands of a human being?

solution.explanation: Each fore limb has the humerus, radius, ulna, 8 carpals (wrist bones), 5 metacarpals (palm bones) and 14 phalanges (digits).
solution.why_others_wrong: 27 is one hand only; 52 uses the 7 tarsals of the foot instead of the 8 carpals; 60 counts all 30 bones of each fore limb.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', appendicular skeleton

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: How many individual ribs in a human are connected ventrally to the sternum, either directly or by joining the seventh rib with the help of hyaline cartilage?

solution.explanation: There are 12 pairs of ribs. The first seven pairs (true ribs) are connected ventrally to the sternum with the help of hyaline cartilage. The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs (vertebrochondral or false ribs) do not articulate directly with the sternum but join the seventh rib with the help of hyaline cartilage. The 11th and 12th pairs (floating ribs) are not connected ventrally.
solution.shortcut: All 24 ribs minus the 4 floating ribs = 20.
solution.why_others_wrong: 14 counts only the true ribs; 10 counts pairs instead of ribs; 24 includes the floating ribs.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', axial skeleton: ribs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a resting sarcomere, the central part of the thick filaments that is not overlapped by the thin filaments is called the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the resting state, the edges of thin filaments on either side of the thick filaments partially overlap the free ends of the thick filaments, leaving the central part of the thick filaments. This central part of the thick filament, not overlapped by thin filaments, is called the H-zone.
steps: Central part of A-band not overlapped by actin → H-zone
solution.why_others_wrong: The I-band contains thin filaments; the Z-line bisects the I-band; the M-line is the fibrous membrane holding the thick filaments together in the middle of the A-band.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', skeletal muscle

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Repeated activation of muscles can lead to fatigue.
Reason (R): Repeated activation leads to the accumulation of lactic acid in muscles due to the anaerobic breakdown of glycogen in them.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: repeated activation of the muscles can lead to the accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic breakdown of glycogen in them, causing fatigue. R gives the cause of A.
steps: R: lactic acid from anaerobic glycogen breakdown → true
Lactic acid accumulation causes the fatigue → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B denies the causal link; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (feature or role).

List-I:
A. Visceral muscles
B. Tropomyosin
C. Heavy meromyosin (HMM)
D. Cilia of the trachea

List-II:
I. Remove dust particles and some foreign substances inhaled with atmospheric air
II. Globular head with a short arm that projects outwards from the myosin filament as a cross arm
III. Protein that runs close to the F-actins throughout their length
IV. Assist in the transportation of food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Muscles, contractile proteins and ciliary movement
solution.explanation: Visceral (smooth) muscles in the walls of hollow organs assist in moving food through the digestive tract and gametes through the genital tract. Two filaments of tropomyosin run close to the F-actins throughout their length. Each meromyosin has a globular head with a short arm (HMM) and a tail (LMM); the HMM projects outwards as the cross arm. Coordinated movements of tracheal cilia remove dust and foreign particles from inhaled air.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap visceral muscle with tropomyosin, tropomyosin with HMM, or HMM with the cilia.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', types of movement; muscle; structure of contractile proteins
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: All movements are locomotions.
Statement II: In Paramecium, cilia help in the movement of food through the cytopharynx and in locomotion.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: all locomotions are movements, but all movements are not locomotions (Statement I false). In Paramecium, cilia help in the movement of food through the cytopharynx and in locomotion (Statement II true).
steps: All locomotions are movements, not the reverse → I false
Paramecium cilia: food movement + locomotion → II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', introduction: movement and locomotion
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the human vertebral column, how many vertebrae lie between the last cervical vertebra and the sacral vertebra?

solution.explanation: The vertebral column of 26 vertebrae is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1, fused) and coccygeal (1, fused) regions, from the skull downwards. Between the last cervical and the sacral vertebra lie the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae.
solution.why_others_wrong: 19 removes only the 7 cervical vertebrae from 26; 12 counts only the thoracic vertebrae; 24 removes only the two fused vertebrae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', axial skeleton: vertebral column

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the mechanism of muscle contraction are correct?

(a) Ca²⁺ binds with a subunit of troponin on the actin filaments and thereby removes the masking of the active sites for myosin.
(b) Muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the CNS via a motor neuron.
(c) The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of a muscle fibre is called the neuromuscular junction or motor-end plate.
(d) The reaction time of the muscle fibres is the same in all muscles.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Contraction is initiated by a CNS signal via a motor neuron; the motor neuron meets the sarcolemma at the neuromuscular junction (motor-end plate). The rise in Ca²⁺ leads to binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin, removing the masking of the active sites for myosin. NCERT notes that the reaction time of the fibres can vary in different muscles.
steps: (d) False: reaction time can vary in different muscles
solution.why_others_wrong: A, B and C include the false statement (d); B and C also leave out true statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Red muscle fibres can also be called aerobic muscles.
Reason (R): Red muscle fibres contain plenty of mitochondria, which can utilise the large amount of oxygen stored in them for ATP production.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: muscles with high myoglobin (a red, oxygen-storing pigment) look reddish and are called red fibres. They contain plenty of mitochondria which can utilise the large amount of oxygen stored in them for ATP production; these muscles, therefore, can also be called aerobic muscles. White fibres have little myoglobin, few mitochondria and much sarcoplasmic reticulum, and depend on anaerobic processes. R explains A.
steps: A: red fibres = aerobic muscles → true
R: many mitochondria using stored O₂ for ATP → true
NCERT links them with 'therefore' → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B denies the link NCERT states; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', mechanism of muscle contraction: red and white fibres
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which statement about the human skull is correct?

options.text: The cranium is made of 14 bones and the facial region of 8 skeletal elements
The skull articulates with the vertebral column through a single occipital condyle

The cranium has 8 bones forming a hard protective outer covering for the brain, the facial region has 14 skeletal elements, and the skull articulates with the vertebral column by two occipital condyles
The first vertebra, the axis, articulates with the occipital condyles

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cranium has 8 bones forming the hard protective outer covering of the brain; the facial region is made of 14 skeletal elements. The skull articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column with the help of two occipital condyles (dicondylic skull). The first vertebra, the atlas, articulates with the occipital condyles.
solution.why_others_wrong: A swaps the cranial and facial counts; B gives one condyle instead of two; D names the axis instead of the atlas.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Locomotion and Movement', axial skeleton: skull
solution.final_answer: Option C: The cranium has 8 bones forming a hard protective outer covering for the brain, the facial region has 14 skeletal elements, and the skull articulates with the vertebral column by two occipital condyles

questions.subject: Zoology

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the thoracic vertebrae, ribs and sternum together form the rib cage (Statement I true). Joints are essential for all types of movements involving the bony parts of the body; force generated by the muscles is used to carry out movement through joints, where the joint acts as a fulcrum (Statement II true).

Joint acts as a fulcrum → II true

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The major part of the human brain is formed by the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the forebrain consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus, and the cerebrum forms the major part of the human brain.
steps: Cerebrum → major part of the human brain
solution.why_others_wrong: The cerebellum and medulla belong to the hindbrain and the thalamus is a forebrain structure that the cerebrum wraps around; none forms the major part.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: forebrain

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane of a neuron is called the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the resting state, the outer surface of the axonal membrane is positive and the inner surface negative (polarised). The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane is called the resting potential.
steps: Resting membrane potential difference → resting potential
solution.why_others_wrong: The action potential (nerve impulse) is the potential difference at a depolarised site; depolarisation is the reversal of polarity, not the resting state.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The midbrain is located between the:

options.text: Medulla oblongata and the spinal cord
Thalamus/hypothalamus of the forebrain and the pons of the hindbrain

solution.explanation: NCERT: the midbrain is located between the thalamus/hypothalamus of the forebrain and the pons of the hindbrain. A canal called the cerebral aqueduct passes through it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The cerebrum and thalamus are both forebrain; the pons and medulla are both hindbrain; the medulla continues into the spinal cord.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: midbrain
solution.final_answer: Option D: Thalamus/hypothalamus of the forebrain and the pons of the hindbrain

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

Cortex thrown into prominent folds → II true

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Transmission of an impulse across an electrical synapse is very similar to impulse conduction along a single axon.
Reason (R): At electrical synapses, the membranes of the pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, and electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: at electrical synapses, the membranes of pre- and post-synaptic neurons are in very close proximity, and electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across these synapses. Transmission of an impulse across them is therefore very similar to conduction along a single axon. R explains A.
steps: A: similar to conduction along one axon → true
R: close membranes, direct current flow → true
Direct current flow makes it like axonal conduction → R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: B denies the explanation; C and D call a true statement false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At a chemical synapse, the arrival of an impulse at the axon terminal stimulates:

options.text: The synthesis of neurotransmitters in the post-synaptic membrane
The movement of synaptic vesicles towards the membrane, where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft
The fusion of the pre- and post-synaptic neurons, closing the synaptic cleft
The direct flow of electrical current into the post-synaptic neuron without any chemical

solution.explanation: NCERT: when an impulse arrives at the axon terminal, it stimulates the movement of the synaptic vesicles towards the membrane, where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release their neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These bind to specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane.
steps: Impulse at terminal → vesicles move and fuse → neurotransmitters released into cleft
solution.why_others_wrong: Neurotransmitters are stored in pre-synaptic vesicles; the cleft is not closed; direct current flow describes an electrical synapse.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', transmission of impulses
solution.final_answer: Option B: The movement of synaptic vesicles towards the membrane, where they fuse with the plasma membrane and release neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the functions of the human brain are correct?

(a) The brain controls the circadian (24-hour) rhythms of our body.
(b) The brain controls the activities of several endocrine glands.
(c) The brain is the site for processing of vision, hearing, speech, memory, intelligence, emotions and thoughts.
(d) Thermoregulation, hunger and thirst are controlled by the brain.
(e) The brain does not control the functioning of vital involuntary organs such as the lungs, heart and kidneys.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the brain is the central information processing organ and acts as the command and control system. It controls voluntary movements, balance, the functioning of vital involuntary organs (lungs, heart, kidneys), thermoregulation, hunger and thirst, circadian rhythms, activities of several endocrine glands and human behaviour, and is the site for processing vision, hearing, speech, memory, intelligence, emotions and thoughts.
steps: (e) False: it controls vital involuntary organs
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B include the false statement (e); D leaves out the true statement (b).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The rise in stimulus-induced permeability to Na⁺ is long-lived and is not followed by any change in the permeability to K⁺.
Statement II: The electrical potential difference across the plasma membrane at a depolarised site is called the action potential, which is in fact termed a nerve impulse.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rise in stimulus-induced permeability to Na⁺ is extremely short-lived; it is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K⁺, and K⁺ diffuses out to restore the resting potential (Statement I false). The potential difference at the depolarised site is the action potential, termed a nerve impulse (Statement II true).
steps: Na⁺ permeability rise is extremely short-lived, then K⁺ permeability rises → I false
Action potential = nerve impulse → II true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The association areas of the cerebral cortex, which are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function, are responsible for:

options.text: Complex functions like intersensory associations, memory and communication
Controlling respiration, cardiovascular reflexes and gastric secretions
Relaying impulses from the CNS to involuntary organs and smooth muscles

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cerebral cortex contains motor areas, sensory areas and large regions that are neither clearly sensory nor motor in function. These regions, called the association areas, are responsible for complex functions like intersensory associations, memory and communication.
steps: Association areas → intersensory associations, memory, communication
solution.why_others_wrong: B is the medulla oblongata, C the autonomic neural system and D the corpus callosum.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: forebrain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Complex functions like intersensory associations, memory and communication

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The brain stem forms the connections between the brain and the spinal cord.
Reason (R): The brain stem consists of the cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the brain stem, formed by the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, forms the connections between the brain and the spinal cord. The cerebrum, thalamus and hypothalamus make up the forebrain. A is true; R is false.
steps: A: brain stem links brain and spinal cord → true
R: cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus = forebrain, not brain stem → false
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept the false reason; D calls the true assertion false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', central neural system: hindbrain
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about neurons and nerve fibres are correct?

(a) Afferent nerve fibres transmit impulses from tissues and organs to the CNS.
(b) Efferent nerve fibres transmit regulatory impulses from the CNS to the concerned peripheral tissues and organs.
(c) An unmyelinated nerve fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath around the axon.
(d) The cell body of a neuron contains cytoplasm with typical cell organelles.
(e) The distal end of the axon is unbranched.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The PNS has afferent fibres (tissues/organs → CNS) and efferent fibres (CNS → peripheral tissues/organs). An unmyelinated fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell that does not form a myelin sheath. The cell body contains cytoplasm with typical cell organelles and Nissl's granules. The axon is a long fibre whose distal end is branched, each branch ending in a synaptic knob.
steps: (e) False: the distal end of the axon is branched
solution.why_others_wrong: A, C and D include the false statement (e); A and C also leave out true statements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', human neural system; neuron as structural and functional unit

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The neural system provides chemical integration through hormones.
Reason (R): The endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the neural system provides an organised network of point-to-point connections for quick coordination, while the endocrine system provides chemical integration through hormones. A wrongly assigns hormonal integration to the neural system, so A is false; R is true.
steps: Neural system → point-to-point, quick coordination → A false
solution.why_others_wrong: A and B accept a false assertion; C calls the true reason false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', introduction: neural system
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: At a site of excitation on an axon, K⁺ diffuses out after the brief rise in Na⁺ permeability and the resting potential is restored within a fraction of a second. The fibre then:

options.text: Remains depolarised, with its inner surface positive
Becomes once more responsive to further stimulation
Releases neurotransmitters along its entire length

solution.explanation: NCERT: the rise in Na⁺ permeability is quickly followed by a rise in K⁺ permeability. Within a fraction of a second, K⁺ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential at the site of excitation, and the fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation.
steps: Na⁺ in (brief) → K⁺ out → resting potential restored
solution.why_others_wrong: Restoring the resting potential ends depolarisation; the membrane can again become permeable to Na⁺; neurotransmitters are released only at axon terminals.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Neural Control and Coordination', generation and conduction of nerve impulse
solution.final_answer: Option C: Becomes once more responsive to further stimulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Anatomically, the pituitary gland is divided into an adenohypophysis and a neurohypophysis. The adenohypophysis consists of which two portions?

solution.explanation: The adenohypophysis consists of two portions, the pars distalis and the pars intermedia. The neurohypophysis is the pars nervosa (posterior pituitary).
solution.why_others_wrong: The pars nervosa is the neurohypophysis, not a part of the adenohypophysis; the hypothalamus is part of the brain, not of the pituitary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Pars distalis and pars intermedia

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: An endocrine gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues; each follicle consists of follicular cells enclosing a cavity, and iodine is essential for the normal rate of its hormone synthesis. The gland is the:

solution.explanation: The thyroid gland is composed of follicles and stromal tissues. Each thyroid follicle is made of follicular cells enclosing a cavity; these cells synthesise thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3). Iodine is essential for the normal rate of thyroid hormone synthesis.
steps: Follicles of follicular cells around a cavity
solution.why_others_wrong: None of the other glands is built of follicles around a cavity or depends on iodine for its hormones.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The adrenal gland is composed of two types of tissues. Which of the following correctly describes their arrangement?

options.text: The adrenal medulla is centrally located and the adrenal cortex lies outside it
The adrenal cortex is centrally located and the adrenal medulla lies outside it
The adrenal medulla and adrenal cortex lie side by side as two lobes joined by an isthmus
The adrenal medulla forms the outermost layer, the zona glomerulosa

solution.explanation: The centrally located tissue of the adrenal gland is the adrenal medulla; the adrenal cortex lies outside it.
solution.why_others_wrong: The cortex surrounds the medulla, not the reverse; an isthmus joins the two lobes of the thyroid; the zona glomerulosa is the outer layer of the cortex, not the medulla.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option A: The adrenal medulla is centrally located and the adrenal cortex lies outside it

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors. These receptors are located:

options.text: In every cell of the body
Only in the endocrine gland that secretes the hormone
Only in the blood plasma, which carries the hormone

solution.explanation: NCERT states that hormones produce their effects by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors, which are located in the target tissues only.
steps: They are present in the target tissues only
solution.why_others_wrong: If every cell had the receptor, every cell would be a target; the secreting gland and the blood carry the hormone but are not where its receptors lie.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Mechanism of hormone action
solution.final_answer: Option B: In the target tissues only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, can result in a condition called acromegaly. This condition is characterised by:

options.text: Excessive loss of water in urine and dehydration
Severe disfigurement, especially of the face

solution.explanation: Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults, especially in middle age, can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called acromegaly. It may lead to serious complications and premature death if unchecked.
steps: Severe disfigurement, especially of the face = acromegaly
solution.why_others_wrong: Stunted growth is pituitary dwarfism (low GH); protruding eyeballs and weight loss describe exophthalmic goitre; excessive water loss describes diabetes insipidus (ADH problem).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option D: Severe disfigurement, especially of the face

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (action).

List-I:
A. Vasopressin
B. FSH (in females)
C. LH (in females)
D. TSH

List-II:
I. Stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles
II. Stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules of the kidney
III. Stimulates synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland
IV. Induces ovulation of fully mature (Graafian) follicles and maintains the corpus luteum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules (hence ADH). In females, FSH stimulates growth and development of the ovarian follicles, while LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles and maintains the corpus luteum. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping FSH and LH ignores that FSH grows follicles while LH triggers ovulation; vasopressin acts on the kidney, not the thyroid, and TSH acts on the thyroid, not the kidney.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about parathyroid hormone (PTH) are correct?

(a) PTH acts on bones and stimulates bone resorption (dissolution/demineralisation).
(b) PTH stimulates the reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules.
(c) PTH increases the absorption of Ca²⁺ from the digested food.
(d) The secretion of PTH is regulated by the circulating level of TSH.
(e) PTH is a steroid hormone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PTH is a peptide hormone that raises blood Ca²⁺: it stimulates bone resorption, reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by the renal tubules and Ca²⁺ absorption from digested food. Its secretion is regulated by the circulating levels of calcium ions, not by TSH.
steps: (d) False: regulated by blood Ca²⁺ level
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with (d) or (e) is wrong: PTH secretion follows blood calcium, and PTH is a peptide, not a steroid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Parathyroid gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Besides regulating the 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of the body, melatonin from the pineal gland also influences:

(a) Metabolism
(b) Pigmentation
(c) The menstrual cycle
(d) Our defence capability
(e) The level of calcium in the blood

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: melatonin regulates the diurnal rhythm and also influences metabolism, pigmentation, the menstrual cycle and our defence capability. Blood calcium is regulated by PTH and thyrocalcitonin, not melatonin.
steps: (e) is the job of PTH and TCT
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing (e) wrongly add calcium regulation; '(c) and (d) only' leaves out metabolism and pigmentation, which NCERT lists.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Pineal gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Cancer of the thyroid gland or development of nodules in it may lead to hyperthyroidism, which adversely affects the body physiology.
Reason (R): Hyperthyroidism is caused by a deficiency of iodine in the diet.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cancer of the thyroid gland or development of thyroid nodules may lead to abnormally high levels of thyroid hormone synthesis (hyperthyroidism), which adversely affects body physiology. Iodine deficiency instead causes hypothyroidism and enlargement of the thyroid (goitre).
steps: R: false - iodine deficiency gives hypothyroidism/goitre
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options A and B are wrong; A is an NCERT statement, so D is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A pregnant woman suffers from untreated hypothyroidism. Which set of features is the developing baby most likely to show?

options.text: Protruding eyeballs, increased basal metabolic rate and weight loss
Stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism
Excessive urination and thirst due to impaired ADH release

solution.explanation: Hypothyroidism during pregnancy causes defective development and maturation of the growing baby, leading to stunted growth (cretinism), mental retardation, low intelligence quotient, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism.
steps: Maternal hypothyroidism -> defective development of the baby
Features: stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin, deaf-mutism
solution.why_others_wrong: Protruding eyeballs with high BMR is hyperthyroidism (Graves' disease); gigantism comes from excess GH; excessive urination from ADH deficiency is diabetes insipidus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The thyroid gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Stunted growth, mental retardation, low IQ, abnormal skin and deaf-mutism

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The adrenal cortex secretes many hormones, commonly called corticoids.
Statement II: The corticoids that are involved in carbohydrate metabolism are called mineralocorticoids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The adrenal cortex secretes corticoids. Those involved in carbohydrate metabolism are glucocorticoids (e.g. cortisol); those that regulate the balance of water and electrolytes are mineralocorticoids (e.g. aldosterone).
steps: Statement II: false - carbohydrate metabolism = glucocorticoids
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II swaps the two classes of corticoids, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is the NCERT definition, so it is not false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Besides producing ova, the ovary also functions as an endocrine gland.
Reason (R): The ovary produces two groups of steroid hormones called estrogen and progesterone.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The ovary is the primary female sex organ that produces one ovum in each menstrual cycle. It is also an endocrine gland because it produces two groups of steroid hormones, estrogen and progesterone.
steps: Secreting hormones is what makes the ovary an endocrine gland, so R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives exactly why the ovary counts as an endocrine gland, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Gonads
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (action).

List-I:
A. Estrogens
B. Glucagon
C. Adrenaline and noradrenaline
D. Progesterone

List-II:
I. Supports pregnancy
II. Increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection (raising of hairs) and sweating
III. Stimulate the growth and activities of the female secondary sex organs
IV. Acts mainly on hepatocytes and stimulates glycogenolysis, raising the blood sugar

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Actions of hormones of the adrenal, pancreas and gonads
solution.explanation: Estrogens stimulate the growth and activities of female secondary sex organs; glucagon acts mainly on liver cells and stimulates glycogenolysis, causing hyperglycemia; catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) increase alertness, pupillary dilation, piloerection and sweating; progesterone supports pregnancy.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping estrogens and progesterone confuses the follicle hormone with the pregnancy-supporting hormone; glucagon acts on hepatocytes, while piloerection and pupillary dilation are emergency effects of catecholamines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The adrenal gland; Pancreas; Testis and ovary
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the pituitary gland are correct?

(a) The pars distalis region is commonly called the anterior pituitary.
(b) The neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) is also known as the posterior pituitary.
(c) The pars distalis produces GH, PRL, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH.
(d) Oxytocin is produced by the pars distalis.
(e) Growth hormone is stored in and released from the neurohypophysis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Regions of the pituitary and their hormones
solution.explanation: The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) produces GH, prolactin, TSH, ACTH, LH and FSH. The neurohypophysis (pars nervosa, posterior pituitary) stores and releases oxytocin and vasopressin, which are synthesised by the hypothalamus. GH is an anterior pituitary hormone.
steps: (d) False: oxytocin is made by the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary
(e) False: the neurohypophysis stores oxytocin and vasopressin, not GH
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) puts oxytocin in the wrong lobe and (e) puts GH in the wrong lobe, so every option containing either is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about hormonal disorders are correct?

(a) Acromegaly is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features become noticeable.
(b) In adult women, hypothyroidism may cause the menstrual cycle to become irregular.
(c) Diabetes insipidus results from a deficiency of insulin.
(d) Patients with diabetes mellitus are successfully treated with insulin therapy.
(e) A low level of ADH increases water reabsorption by the kidney, so very little urine is formed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Acromegaly is hard to diagnose early and often goes undetected for years. Hypothyroidism in adult women may make the menstrual cycle irregular. Diabetes insipidus is due to impaired synthesis or release of ADH, which causes excessive loss of water (diuresis), not water retention. Diabetes mellitus (insulin-related) is successfully treated with insulin therapy.
steps: (e) False: low ADH reduces water reabsorption and causes diuresis
solution.why_others_wrong: (c) mixes up diabetes insipidus (ADH) with diabetes mellitus (insulin); (e) reverses the effect of low ADH; every other option includes one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland; The thyroid gland; Pancreas

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In males, LH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis.
Statement II: Growth hormone is secreted by the pars intermedia of the pituitary.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In males, FSH (not LH) and androgens regulate spermatogenesis; LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens. Growth hormone is secreted by the pars distalis; the pars intermedia secretes only MSH.
steps: Statement I: false - FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis
Statement II: false - GH is from the pars distalis
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements carry a swapped name (LH for FSH, pars intermedia for pars distalis), so any option calling either true is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', The pituitary gland
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the gonads are correct?

(a) The ovary is composed of ovarian follicles and stromal tissues.
(b) Progesterone is the hormone secreted mainly by the growing ovarian follicles before ovulation.
(c) After ovulation, the ruptured follicle is converted into the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone.
(d) The testis performs dual functions, as a primary sex organ and as an endocrine gland.
(e) The Leydig cells are located inside the seminiferous tubules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Testis and ovary as endocrine glands
solution.explanation: The ovary has ovarian follicles and stromal tissues; growing follicles secrete estrogen, and after ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes mainly progesterone. The testis is both a primary sex organ and an endocrine gland; it has seminiferous tubules and stromal (interstitial) tissue, and the Leydig cells lie in the intertubular spaces.
steps: (e) False: Leydig cells are in the intertubular (interstitial) spaces
solution.why_others_wrong: (b) gives the growing follicles the corpus luteum's hormone; (e) puts the Leydig cells inside the tubules; every other option contains one of them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, Ch 19 'Chemical Coordination and Integration', Testis and ovary

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In human males, the seminal plasma together with the sperms constitutes the:

solution.explanation: The secretions of the male accessory glands form the seminal plasma. The seminal plasma along with the sperms constitutes the semen.
solution.why_others_wrong: Colostrum is the early milk of lactation; amniotic fluid surrounds the foetus; the antrum is the fluid-filled cavity of the tertiary follicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Each human testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm. Its width is about:

solution.explanation: NCERT: each testis is oval in shape, with a length of about 4 to 5 cm and a width of about 2 to 3 cm.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10-12 cm is the length of an oviduct; the width cannot exceed the 4-5 cm length; 0.2-0.3 cm is far too small.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The male reproductive system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules. This release is called:

solution.explanation: Spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis. The sperm heads then become embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation.
steps: Release of sperms from the tubules = spermiation
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermiogenesis is the change of spermatids into sperms, which happens before release; insemination is the release of semen into the vagina; ovulation is the release of the ovum from the ovary.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The mitotic divisions (cleavage) of the human zygote as it moves towards the uterus form 2, 4, 8 and 16 daughter cells. These daughter cells are called:

solution.explanation: Cleavage starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus and forms 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres.
steps: Cleavage = mitotic divisions of the zygote
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermatids come from meiosis in the testis; polar bodies come from the unequal meiotic divisions of the oocyte; granulosa cells surround the oocyte in the follicle.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The shape of the human uterus is like:

solution.explanation: The uterus is single and is also called the womb. Its shape is like an inverted pear, and it is supported by ligaments attached to the pelvic wall.
solution.why_others_wrong: The funnel with fimbriae is the infundibulum of the oviduct; a coiled tube describes the seminiferous tubule; the uterus has no bean-like shape.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the secretions of which of the following are essential for the maturation and motility of sperms?

options.text: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate

solution.concept: Role of male accessory ducts and glands
solution.explanation: Sperms released from the seminiferous tubules are transported by the accessory ducts. The secretions of the epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate are essential for the maturation and motility of sperms.
steps: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate
Their secretions -> maturation and motility of sperms
solution.why_others_wrong: Ovary, oviduct and uterus are female organs; Leydig cells secrete androgens into the blood, not secretions for sperm maturation; the urinary bladder and ureters belong to the excretory system.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle and prostate

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length and is connected to the pelvic wall and the uterus by ligaments.
Statement II: The uterus is single and is also called the womb.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length and is connected to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments. The uterus is single and is also called the womb.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT descriptions, so options calling either false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the structure of a human sperm are correct?

(a) A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of the sperm.
(b) The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus.
(c) The sperm is made up of a head, neck, middle piece and tail.
(d) The tail of the sperm contains numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for its movement.
(e) The acrosome covers the posterior portion of the sperm head.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A sperm is a microscopic structure made of a head, neck, middle piece and tail; a plasma membrane envelops the whole body. The head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like acrosome. The middle piece (not the tail) has numerous mitochondria that produce energy for the tail's movement.
steps: (d) False: mitochondria are in the middle piece
(e) False: the acrosome covers the anterior portion
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) moves the mitochondria to the tail and (e) moves the acrosome to the back of the head, so every option with either is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The endometrium of the uterus is maintained during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle.
Reason (R): The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the luteal phase the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of progesterone. Progesterone is essential for maintaining the endometrium, which is needed for implantation of a fertilised ovum.
steps: Progesterone from the corpus luteum is the reason the endometrium is maintained
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives the cause of A, so B is wrong; both statements are true, so C and D are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of the normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause.
Statement II: The secretion of the gonadotropins (LH and FSH) decreases gradually during the follicular phase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: cyclic menstruation indicates the normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause. During the follicular phase the secretion of gonadotropins increases gradually, stimulating follicular development and estrogen secretion by the growing follicles.
steps: Statement II: false - gonadotropins increase gradually in the follicular phase
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses the trend of LH and FSH, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is an NCERT line, so options calling it false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (phase of the menstrual cycle) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Menstrual phase
B. Follicular phase
C. Ovulatory phase
D. Luteal phase

List-II:
I. Remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum
II. Breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels when the ovum is not fertilised
III. Primary follicles grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle
IV. Rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The menstrual phase is the breakdown of the endometrial lining and its blood vessels (when the ovum is not fertilised). In the follicular phase, primary follicles grow into a fully mature Graafian follicle. In the ovulatory phase, the Graafian follicle ruptures and releases the ovum. In the luteal phase, the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle form the corpus luteum.
solution.why_others_wrong: Follicle growth precedes and ovulation follows it, so swapping B and C is wrong; the corpus luteum forms after ovulation, not during menstruation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual cycle
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The mammary glands of a female differentiate during pregnancy. They start producing milk:

options.text: From the first month of pregnancy
Only from puberty onwards, in every menstrual cycle

solution.explanation: NCERT: the mammary glands of the female undergo differentiation during pregnancy and start producing milk towards the end of pregnancy by the process called lactation.
steps: Milk production begins: towards the end of pregnancy
solution.why_others_wrong: Milk production does not start early in pregnancy or in non-pregnant cycles; the initial milk (colostrum) is already available in the first days after birth, so it does not begin weeks later.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Parturition and lactation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Towards the end of pregnancy

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens).
Reason (R): Androgens are synthesised and secreted by the Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubules.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT states that the functions of the male sex accessory ducts and glands are maintained by the testicular hormones (androgens). Androgens are secreted by the Leydig (interstitial) cells in the intertubular spaces; the Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.
steps: R: false - androgens come from the Leydig cells
solution.why_others_wrong: R is false, so options A and B are wrong; A is an NCERT statement, so D is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis (spermatogenesis); The male reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following shows the correct order of the parts of a human oviduct, starting from the end nearer the ovary?

solution.explanation: Each oviduct extends from the periphery of the ovary to the uterus. The part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum; it leads to the wider ampulla; the last part, the isthmus, has a narrow lumen and joins the uterus.
steps: Last, narrow part joining the uterus: isthmus
solution.why_others_wrong: The isthmus is the last part joining the uterus, not the first; the infundibulum, not the ampulla, is closest to the ovary; the ampulla lies between the infundibulum and the isthmus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The female reproductive system
solution.final_answer: Option B: Infundibulum → ampulla → isthmus → uterus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: During fertilisation in humans, the secretions of the acrosome help the sperm to:

options.text: Block the entry of additional sperms into the ovum
Attach the blastocyst to the endometrium
Produce energy for the movement of the tail
Enter the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane

solution.concept: Role of the acrosome in fertilisation
solution.explanation: The secretions of the acrosome help the sperm enter into the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane. The block to additional sperms comes from changes in the zona pellucida membrane.
steps: Acrosome = enzyme-filled cap on the sperm head
Its secretions let the sperm pass the zona pellucida and plasma membrane into the ovum's cytoplasm
solution.why_others_wrong: Blocking extra sperms is done by changes in the zona pellucida; attachment to the endometrium is done by the trophoblast; energy for the tail comes from mitochondria in the middle piece.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and implantation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Enter the cytoplasm of the ovum through the zona pellucida and the plasma membrane

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
